value.zh: 虞世南與論人物，始言江左、山東，尚相酬對；
value.en: Yu Shinan debated men of talent with him; when they began with the Jiangzuo and Shandong regions, they could still hold their own in exchange;
value.literal: Yu Shinan discussed with him the evaluation of men; at first speaking of the Jiangzuo and Shandong regions, they still matched wits in reply;

value.zh: 至北地，則笑而不答，歎曰：「肉譜定可畏。」
value.en: but when the talk turned to the north, Shousu only laughed and kept silent; Shinan sighed and said, "The Meat Genealogy is truly formidable."
value.literal: when it came to the northern regions, [Shousu] merely laughed and did not answer; [Shinan] sighed and said: "The Meat Genealogy is truly formidable."

value.zh: 許敬宗曰：「倉曹此名，豈雅目邪？
value.en: Xu Jingzong said, "This nickname for the warehouse clerk -- is it a refined one?
value.literal: Xu Jingzong said: "This name for the warehouse clerk -- is it an elegant title?

value.zh: 宜有以更之。」
value.en: Surely something better ought to replace it."
value.literal: There ought to be something to replace it."

value.zh: 世南曰：「昔任彥升通經，時稱'五經笥'，今以倉曹為'人物志'，可乎？」
value.en: Shinan said, "In olden days Ren Yansheng mastered the classics and was called the 'Casket of the Five Classics'; might we call the warehouse clerk the 'Record of Persons' -- would that serve?"
value.literal: Shinan said: "In former times Ren Yansheng mastered the classics and was styled the 'Casket of the Five Classics'; might we style the warehouse clerk the 'Record of Persons' -- would that do?"

value.zh: 時渭州刺史李淹亦明譜學，守素所論，惟淹能抗之。
value.en: At that time Li Yan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was also learned in genealogy; of Shousu's arguments, only Yan could stand against him.
value.literal: At that time Li Yan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was also versed in genealogical studies; of Shousu's disquisitions, only Yan could contend with him.

value.zh: 姚思廉，本名簡，以字行，陳吏部尚書察之子。
value.en: Yao Silian, whose original name was Jian, went by his courtesy name; he was the son of Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel under Chen.
value.literal: Yao Silian, original name Jian, used his courtesy name in public; he was the son of Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel under Chen.

value.zh: 陳亡，察自吳興遷京兆，遂為萬年人。
value.en: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing to the capital district and became a man of Wannian.
value.literal: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing to Jingzhao and thus became a man of Wannian.

value.zh: 思廉少受《漢書》於察，盡傳其業。
value.en: Silian studied the 《Book of Han》 under Cha in his youth and wholly inherited his father's craft.
value.literal: Silian in youth received the 《Book of Han》 from Cha and fully inherited his work.

value.zh: 寡嗜欲，惟一於學，未嘗問家人生貲。
value.en: He cared little for pleasure, gave himself wholly to study, and never once asked after his family's means.
value.literal: He had few desires, devoted himself solely to learning, and never inquired after his household's livelihood or property.

value.zh: 武平一，名甄，以字行，潁川郡王載德子也。
value.en: Wu Pingyi, whose personal name was Zhen but who went by his courtesy name, was the son of Prince Zaidel of Yingchuan.
value.literal: Wu Pingyi—Wu Pingyi's given name was Zhen; he was known by his style name; he was a son of Prince Zaidel of Yingchuan Commandery.

value.zh: 博學，通《春秋》，工文辭。
value.en: He was erudite, thoroughly versed in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, and skilled in literary writing.
value.literal: He was broadly learned, mastered the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, and excelled at literary composition.

value.zh: 武后時，畏禍不敢與事，隱嵩山修浮圖法，屢詔不應。
value.en: During Empress Wu's reign, fearing trouble he avoided public office, withdrew to Mount Song to study Buddhist teachings, and declined repeated imperial calls.
value.literal: In Empress Wu's time, fearing calamity he dared not take part in affairs; he retired to Mount Song to practice Buddhist dharma, and repeatedly ignored imperial summons.

value.zh: 中宗復位，平一居母喪，迫召為起居舍人，丐終制，不見聽。
value.en: After Zhongzong's restoration, Pingyi was observing mourning for his mother when he was pressed to serve as Attendant of the Imperial Diary; he pleaded to finish his mourning obligations, but the court would not grant it.
value.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, Pingyi was in mourning for his mother; he was urgently summoned as Attendant of the Imperial Diary, begged to complete the mourning period, and was not heeded.

value.zh: 景龍二年，兼修文館直學士。
value.en: In Jinglong year 2 he was also appointed a direct academician of the Palace Library Institute.
value.literal: In the second year of Jinglong, he was concurrently made a direct academician of the Xiūwén Guan.

value.zh: 時天子暗柔不君，韋後蒸亂，外戚盛。
value.en: The emperor had grown dim and pliant, no longer truly ruling; Empress Wei stirred scandal and disorder, and the power of the imperial in-laws swelled unchecked.
value.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was dim and yielding and did not rule as sovereign; Empress Wei brought chaos through illicit relations, and the maternal kin flourished.

value.zh: 平一重斥語，即自請抑母黨，上言：「去歲熒惑入羽林，太白再經天，太陽虧，月犯大角。
value.en: Ping Yi had already spoken blunt rebukes; he now volunteered to curb his mother's faction and memorialized the throne: "Last year Mars entered the Feathered Guard, Venus crossed the sky twice, the sun suffered eclipse, and the moon struck Great Horn.
value.literal: Ping Yi repeatedly spoke words of harsh rebuke, and immediately requested of himself to restrain his mother's faction, submitting a memorial: "Last year Mars entered the Forest of Feathers, the Great White Star twice crossed the heavens, the sun was eclipsed, and the moon encroached upon Great Horn.

value.zh: 臣聞災不妄生，上見下應，信如景響。
value.en: I have heard that disasters do not arise without reason: heaven shows a sign, and earth answers below, as surely as an echo follows a sound.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that calamities do not arise without cause; what appears above, responds below — as surely as shadow follows form.

value.zh: 《詩》曰：'唯此文王，小心翼翼，昭事上帝，聿懷多福。
value.en: The Book of Odes says: 'Only this King Wen — careful and reverent, serving Heaven with clear devotion — thereby gathered many blessings.'
value.literal: The Book of Odes says: 'Only this King Wen, with meticulous care, clearly served God on high, and thereby harbored many blessings.'

value.zh: '陛下天性孝愛，戚屬外家，恩洽澤濡。
value.en: Your Majesty is filial and loving by nature; toward your maternal kin you have poured out favor until it runs deep.
value.literal: Your Majesty's nature is filial and loving; toward relatives of the outer family, grace has penetrated and blessings have soaked them through.

value.zh: 臣一宗，階三等，家數侯，硃輪華轂，過許、史、梁、鄧遠甚。
value.en: My clan alone holds third-rank posts; several of us are enfeoffed as marquises, riding in vermillion-wheeled carriages with gilded hubs — honors surpassing by far those once granted the Xu, Shi, Liang, and Deng clans.
value.literal: Your servant's one clan holds rank of the third grade; several in the family are marquises, with vermillion wheels and decorated hubs — far exceeding the Xu, Shi, Liang, and Deng families of old.

value.zh: 恩崇者議積，位厚者釁速，故月滿必虧，日中則移，時不再來，榮難久藉。
value.en: Where favor runs high, resentment gathers; where rank sits heavy, ruin comes fast. The full moon must wane, the noon sun must move — time does not return, and splendor cannot be held forever.
value.literal: Those who receive great favor accumulate blame; those who hold weighty rank invite disaster quickly. Thus when the moon is full it must wane, when the sun stands at noon it shifts — time does not return, and glory cannot long be borrowed.

value.zh: 昔永淳之後，王室多難，先聖從權，故臣家以宗子竊祿疏封。
value.en: After the Yongchun reign the house of Tang knew many trials; the late emperor, acting from necessity, allowed our collateral line to hold stipends and distant fiefs we had no true right to claim.
value.literal: In the past after the Yongchun era the royal house suffered many troubles; the former sage exercised expedient measures, so my family, as collateral descendants, improperly received salaries and distant enfeoffments.

value.zh: 今上聖復辟，宜退守園廬，乃再假光寵，爵封如初，高班厚位，遂超涯極。
value.en: Now that Your Majesty has restored order to the realm, we should have retired to our country estates — yet once more we were showered with honors, titles and fiefs restored as before, until rank and reward passed every proper limit.
value.literal: Now that the sagely sovereign has restored the throne, we ought to withdraw and keep to our estates — yet again radiant favor was granted, titles and enfeoffments as before, high ranks and thick positions exceeding all bounds.

value.zh: 故陰氣僭陽，河、洛泛溢。
value.en: Yin overstepped yang; the Yellow and Luo rivers burst their banks.
value.literal: Hence yin energy usurped yang; the Yellow and Luo Rivers overflowed their banks.

value.zh: 昔王族驕盈，梅福上書；
value.en: In former times, when the imperial clan grew proud and overbearing, Mei Fu submitted a memorial;
value.literal: In antiquity when the royal clan grew arrogant and full, Mei Fu submitted a memorial;

value.zh: 竇氏專縱，丁鴻進諫。
value.en: when the Dou clan ruled without restraint, Ding Hong dared to remonstrate.
value.literal: when the Dou clan acted with unchecked license, Ding Hong offered remonstrance.

value.zh: 且後妃之家，恩過寵深，一朝覆沒，遂無噍類。
value.en: And the households of empresses and consorts, though once drowned in favor, have in a single day been overturned and destroyed, until not one soul remained.
value.literal: Moreover the families of empresses and consorts — when favor exceeded all bounds and indulgence ran deep — in a single morning were overthrown and wiped out, leaving not one survivor.

value.zh: 願思仰損之宜、長遠之策，推遠時權，以全親親。」
value.en: I beg you to weigh the wisdom of humble restraint and far-sighted policy — to set aside present advantage for the sake of kinship itself."
value.literal: I pray Your Majesty will consider the fitness of upward self-diminishment and long-term strategy, push away temporary power, and thereby preserve the closeness of kin."

value.zh: 帝慰勉，不許。
value.en: The emperor comforted and praised him, but would not agree.
value.literal: The Emperor comforted and encouraged him, but did not consent.

value.zh: 遷考功員外郎。
value.en: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
value.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 居易被遇憲宗時，事無不言，湔剔抉摩，多見聽可，然為當路所忌，遂擯斥，所蘊不能施，乃放意文酒。
value.en: In the days when Bai Juyi enjoyed Emperor Xianzong's trust, he held nothing back—scrubbing and probing every fault he found, and much of what he said was heeded. Yet those in power resented him, and he was driven out. Unable to put his talents to use, he surrendered himself to literature and wine.
value.literal: When Bai Juyi enjoyed Emperor Xianzong's favor, nothing went unsaid—he scrubbed and probed every issue, and much was heeded; yet those in power envied him, and he was cast aside. What he held within could not be applied, so he gave himself over to letters and wine.

value.zh: 既復用，又皆幼君，偃蹇益不合，居官輒病去，遂無立功名意。
value.en: When he was recalled to service, the emperors were all young men, and his stubborn integrity suited them less and less. Each time he took office he soon pleaded illness and withdrew, until at last he abandoned all thought of establishing a lasting name.
value.literal: When brought back to office, the emperors were all young; his unyielding manner fit less and less. Each time he took office he soon pleaded illness and left—eventually he lost all ambition for lasting achievement.

value.zh: 與弟行簡、從祖弟敏中友愛。
value.en: He was devoted to his younger brother Xingjian and his cousin Minzhong.
value.literal: He was deeply affectionate with his younger brother Xingjian and his paternal cousin Minzhong.

value.zh: 東都所居履道裏，疏詔種樹，構石樓香山，鑿八節灘，自號醉吟先生，為之傳。
value.en: At his home in Luadao Lane in the Eastern Capital, he cleared land and planted trees, built a stone pavilion on Mount Xiangshan, and cut the Eight-Rapids channel. He styled himself the Master of Drunken Chanting and wrote an account of that life.
value.literal: At his residence in Luadao Lane in the Eastern Capital, he cleared ground and planted trees, built a stone pavilion on Mount Xiangshan, excavated the Eight-Rapids shoal, styled himself the Master of Drunken Chanting, and wrote a biography of that life.

value.zh: 暮節惑浮屠道尤甚，至經月不食葷，稱香山居士。
value.en: In his later years he was drawn ever more deeply to Buddhism, abstaining from meat for months at a time, and styled himself Lay Buddhist of Mount Xiangshan.
value.literal: In his later years he was especially drawn to Buddhism, going whole months without eating meat, and styled himself Lay Buddhist of Mount Xiangshan.

value.zh: 嘗與胡杲、吉旼、鄭據、劉真、盧真、張渾、狄兼謨、盧貞燕集，皆高年不事者，人慕之，繪為《九老圖》。
value.en: He once held festive gatherings with Hu Gao, Ji Min, Zheng Ju, Liu Zhen, Lu Zhen, Zhang Hun, Di Jianmo, and Lu Zhen—all elderly men who had withdrawn from office. Admiring them, people painted The Picture of the Nine Elders.
value.literal: He once gathered for banquets with Hu Gao, Ji Min, Zheng Ju, Liu Zhen, Lu Zhen, Zhang Hun, Di Jianmo, and Lu Zhen—all advanced in years and retired from office. People admired them, and painted The Picture of the Nine Elders.

value.zh: 李烏王楊曹高劉石
value.en: Li, Wu, Wang, Yang, Cao, Gao, Liu, and Shi
value.literal: Li, Wu, Wang, Yang, Cao, Gao, Liu, Shi

value.zh: 子逢，從父征伐，累功署忠武都知兵馬使。
value.en: His son Feng campaigned with him, won repeated honors, and was appointed overall commander of the Zhongwu army.
value.literal: His son Feng followed his father in campaigns, accumulated merit, and was appointed overall commander of Zhongwu military affairs.

value.zh: 太和中，入為諸衛將軍。
value.en: During the Taihe era he entered court service as a guard general.
value.literal: In the Taihe era he entered court as a general of the guard regiments.

value.zh: 從劉沔、石雄破回鶻於天德，有士二千人未嘗戰，欲冒賞賜，逢不與。
value.en: He followed Liu Mian and Shi Xiong in defeating the Uyghurs at Tiande; two thousand men who had never fought demanded rewards anyway, and Feng refused.
value.literal: Following Liu Mian and Shi Xiong he defeated the Uyghurs at Tiande; there were two thousand soldiers who had never fought yet wished to claim rewards fraudulently — Feng would not grant them.

value.zh: 或為請之，答曰：「士奮死取賞，若無功而賞，何哉？」
value.en: When others interceded for them he replied, "Men risk death for reward — what becomes of discipline if the idle are paid?"
value.literal: Some pleaded for them; he answered: "Soldiers strive to death to win reward — if without merit there is reward, what then?"

value.zh: 武宗以逢用法嚴，使宰相李德裕讓之，逢曰：「戰者，前踏白刃，不以法，人孰用命？」
value.en: Emperor Wuzong, finding Feng too strict, had Chancellor Li Deyu rebuke him. Feng answered, "In battle men face naked steel — without discipline, who will give his life?"
value.literal: Emperor Wuzong, because Feng applied the law strictly, had Chancellor Li Deyu reprove him. Feng said: "In battle one treads before naked blades — without law, who will stake his life?"

value.zh: 討劉稹也，為太原道行營將，領陳許兵七千屯翼城。
value.en: In the campaign against Liu Zhen he served on the Taiyuan front, leading seven thousand Chen-Xu troops at Yicheng.
value.literal: Campaigning against Liu Zhen, he was a Taiyuan circuit field camp general, leading seven thousand Chen-Xu troops encamped at Yicheng.

value.zh: 稹平，加檢校右散騎常侍。
value.en: After Zhen's defeat he was made acting Right Gentleman for Casual Conversation.
value.literal: When Zhen was pacified he was made acting Right Gentleman for Casual Conversation.

value.zh: 後亦至忠武節度使雲。
value.en: He later also rose to military commissioner of Zhongwu.
value.literal: Later he also reached the post of Zhongwu military commissioner.

value.zh: 劉稹阻命，詔沔南討，屯榆社。
value.en: When Liu Zhen rebelled Mian was ordered south and encamped at Yushe.
value.literal: Liu Zhen defied orders; an edict ordered Mian south to campaign and encamp at Yushe.

value.zh: 沔素與張仲武不協，時方追幽州兵，故徙義成。
value.en: Mian had long been at odds with Zhang Zhongwu; with Youzhou forces in pursuit he was shifted to Yicheng.
value.literal: Mian had long been at odds with Zhang Zhongwu; at the time they were pursuing Youzhou troops, and therefore he was transferred to Yicheng.

value.zh: 會王宰逗留，宰相李德裕表沔鎮河陽，以滑兵二千壁萬善，居宰肘腋下，激之俾出軍。
value.en: When Wang Zai stalled, Li Deyu had Mian posted at Heyang with two thousand Hua troops at Wanshan to press Zai from the rear and force him forward.
value.literal: It happened that Wang Zai lingered; Chancellor Li Deyu memorialized that Mian garrison Heyang, with two thousand Hua troops fortify Wanshan, sit under Zai's armpit, and stir him to make the army advance.

value.zh: 稹平，進檢校司徒，徙忠武節度使。
value.en: After Zhen's defeat he was promoted to acting Minister of Education and made commissioner of Zhongwu.
value.literal: When Zhen was pacified he was advanced to acting Minister of Education and transferred to military commissioner of Zhongwu.

value.zh: 以病改太子少保，不任謁，拜太子太傅致仕。
value.en: Illness forced him to become Junior Guardian; unable to attend court he was named Grand Tutor and retired.
value.literal: Because of illness he was changed to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, could not perform audiences, and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

value.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈司徒。
value.en: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously honored as Minister of Education.
value.literal: He died at age sixty-five and was posthumously made Minister of Education.

value.zh: 武寧李彥佐討劉稹逗留，以雄為晉絳行營諸軍副使，助彥佐。
value.en: When Li Yanzhuo of Wuning stalled in the campaign against Liu Zhen, Xiong was named vice commander of the Jin-Jiang field armies to assist him.
value.literal: Li Yanzhuo of Wuning, campaigning against Liu Zhen, lingered; Xiong was made vice commander of the Jin-Jiang field camp armies to assist Yanzhuo.

value.zh: 是時，王宰屯萬善，劉沔屯石會關，顧望莫先進。
value.en: Wang Zai held Wanshan and Liu Mian held Shihui Pass; both hung back, neither willing to advance.
value.literal: At this time Wang Zai encamped at Wanshan, Liu Mian at Shihui Pass; they looked about and none advanced first.

value.zh: 雄受命，即勒兵越烏嶺，破賊五壁，斬獲千計，賊大震。
value.en: Xiong took command at once, crossed Wuling, stormed five rebel forts, killed and captured by the thousands, and threw the enemy into panic.
value.literal: Xiong received the order and immediately drove the army over Wuling, broke five rebel ramparts, beheaded and captured by the thousands, and the rebels were greatly shaken.

value.zh: 雄臨財廉，每朝廷賜與，輒置軍門，自取一匹縑，余悉分士伍，由是眾感發，無不奮。
value.en: Scrupulous with money, he placed every imperial gift at the camp gate, kept one bolt of silk for himself, and gave the rest to his men; the army was moved to fight with all their might.
value.literal: Xiong in handling wealth was frugal; whenever the court bestowed gifts he placed them at the army gate, took for himself one bolt of silk, and distributed all the rest among the soldiers; from this the masses were moved and stirred, and none did not strive.

value.zh: 武宗喜曰：「今將帥義而勇罕雄比者。」
value.en: Emperor Wuzong said with delight, "Among today's commanders for loyalty and courage, few can match Xiong."
value.literal: Wuzong said with pleasure: "Among commanders today who are righteous and brave, few can be compared with Xiong."

value.zh: 就拜行營節度使，代彥佐。
value.en: He was immediately made field camp commissioner, replacing Yanzhuo.
value.literal: He was immediately appointed field camp military commissioner, replacing Yanzhuo.

value.zh: 徙河中。
value.en: He was transferred to Hedong.
value.literal: He was transferred to Hedong.

value.zh: 稹危蹙，其大將郭誼密獻款，請斬稹首自歸。
value.en: Zhen was cornered; his general Guo Yi secretly offered surrender, promising to kill Zhen and submit.
value.literal: Zhen was in dire straits; his great general Guo Yi secretly offered allegiance, requesting to behead Zhen and return in submission.

value.zh: 眾疑其詐，雄大言曰：「稹之叛，誼為謀主。
value.en: Some suspected a trick; Xiong declared, "Yi was the chief architect of Zhen's rebellion.
value.literal: The masses suspected deception; Xiong spoke loudly: "In Zhen's rebellion Yi was the chief plotter.

value.zh: 今欲殺稹，乃誼自謀，又何疑？」
value.en: If he now wants Zhen dead, that is his own scheme — why doubt him?"
value.literal: Now wishing to kill Zhen is Yi's own plot — what is there to doubt?"

value.zh: 雄以七千人徑薄潞，受誼降。
value.en: Xiong took seven thousand men straight to Lu and accepted Yi's surrender.
value.literal: Xiong with seven thousand men pressed straight on Lu and accepted Yi's surrender.

value.zh: 進檢校兵部尚書，徙河陽。
value.en: He was promoted to acting Minister of War and transferred to Heyang.
value.literal: He was advanced to acting Minister of War and transferred to Heyang.

value.zh: 初，雄討稹，水次見白鷺，謂眾曰：「使吾射中其目，當成功。」
value.en: Early in the campaign against Zhen he saw a white egret by the river and told his men, "If I hit its eye, we will win."
value.literal: At first, when Xiong campaigned against Zhen, by the water he saw a white egret and told the masses: "If I shoot and hit its eye, we shall succeed."

value.zh: 一發如言。
value.en: One shot struck true.
value.literal: With one shot it was as he said.

value.zh: 帝聞，下詔褒美。
value.en: The emperor heard and issued an edict of praise.
value.literal: The emperor heard and issued an edict praising him.

value.zh: 沙陀，西突厥別部處月種也。
value.en: The Shatuo were a branch of the Chuyue people, a dependent tribe of the Western Turks.
value.literal: The Shatuo were of the Chuyue branch among the dependent tribes of the Western Turks.

value.zh: 始，突厥東西部分治烏孫故地，與處月、處蜜雜居。
value.en: In the beginning, as the Eastern and Western Turks partitioned the old Wusun territories, they dwelt alongside the Chuyue and Chumi peoples.
value.literal: At first, when the Eastern and Western Turks divided rule over the former Wusun lands, they lived intermixed with the Chuyue and Chumi.

value.zh: 貞觀七年，太宗以鼓纛立利邲咄陸可汗，而族人步真觖望，謀並其弟彌射乃自立。
value.en: In Zhenguan 7 (633), Emperor Taizong invested Ashina Yipiduolu as khan in the formal drum-and-banner ceremony. A clansman named Böke, resentful of the appointment, conspired to ally with his younger brother Mishe and seize power for himself.
value.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Taizong installed Ashina Yipiduolu as khan with the drum-and-banner ceremony; the clansman Böke was discontented and plotted to join his younger brother Mishe and declare himself ruler.

value.zh: 彌射懼，率處月等入朝。
value.en: Fearing for his safety, Mishe led the Chuyue and other tribes to present themselves at court.
value.literal: Mishe was afraid and led the Chuyue and others to submit to the court.

value.zh: 而步真勢窮，亦歸國。
value.en: Böke, his position hopeless, likewise submitted to the Tang.
value.literal: Böke, his strength exhausted, also returned to allegiance.

value.zh: 其留者，咄陸以射匱特勒劫越之子賀魯統之。
value.en: Those who stayed behind were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.
value.literal: Those who remained were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.

value.zh: 執宜死，子赤心嗣。
value.en: When Zhuyi died, his son Chixin succeeded him.
value.literal: Zhuyi died; his son Chixin succeeded.

value.zh: 開成四年，回鶻徑磧口，抵榆林塞。
value.en: In Kaicheng 4 (839) the Uyghurs marched straight through the desert pass and reached the Yulin frontier.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng the Uyghurs went straight through the desert pass and reached Yulin frontier.

value.zh: 宰相掘羅勿以良馬三百遺赤心，約共攻彰信可汗。
value.en: Chancellor Jueluowu sent Chixin three hundred fine horses and proposed a joint attack on Khan Zhangxin.
value.literal: Chancellor Jueluowu sent Chixin three hundred fine horses and agreed to attack Khan Zhangxin together.

value.zh: 可汗死，節度使劉沔以沙陀擊回鶻於殺胡山。
value.en: After the khan's death, Military Governor Liu Mian led the Shatuo against the Uyghurs at Shahu Mountain.
value.literal: When the khan died, Military Governor Liu Mian used the Shatuo to strike the Uyghurs at Shahu Mountain.

value.zh: 久之，伐潞，誅劉稹，詔赤心率代北騎軍三千隸石雄為前軍，破石會關，助王宰下天井，合太原軍，次榆社，與監軍使呂義忠禽楊弁。
value.en: Later, in the campaign against Lu to execute Liu Zhen, Chixin was ordered to lead three thousand Northern Dai horsemen under Shi Xiong as the vanguard. They stormed Shihui Pass, helped Wang Zai take Tianjing, joined forces with the Taiyuan army, encamped at Yushe, and together with Army Supervisor Lü Yizhong captured Yang Bian.
value.literal: After a time, campaigning against Lu to execute Liu Zhen, Chixin was ordered to lead three thousand Northern Dai cavalry under Shi Xiong as vanguard; they broke Shihui Pass, helped Wang Zai take Tianjing, joined the Taiyuan army, encamped at Yushe, and with Army Supervisor Lü Yizhong captured Yang Bian.

value.zh: 潞州平，遷朔州刺史，仍為代北軍使。
value.en: After Luzhou was pacified he was transferred to prefect of Shuozhou while retaining command of the Northern Dai army.
value.literal: When Luzhou was pacified, he was moved to prefect of Shuozhou and remained Northern Dai army commander.

value.zh: 呂思誠
value.en: Lu Sicheng
value.literal: Lu Sicheng

value.zh: 汪澤民，字叔志，徽之婺源州人，宋端明殿學士藻之七世孫也。
value.en: Wang Zemin (Shuzhi), a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou, was the seventh-generation descendant of the Song academician Wang Zao of the Duanming Hall.
value.literal: Wang Zemin, courtesy name Shuzhi, was a native of Wuyuan Prefecture in Huizhou, seventh-generation descendant of the Song Duanming Hall Academician Wang Zao.

value.zh: 少警悟，家貧力學，既長，遂通諸經。
value.en: Clever and keen from boyhood, he studied hard despite poverty; in adulthood he had mastered the full canon of classics.
value.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive; though his family was poor he studied with tireless effort, and once grown he mastered all the Classics.

value.zh: 延祐初，以《春秋》中鄉貢，上禮部，下第，授寧國路儒學正。
value.en: Early in Yanyou he qualified in the provincial examinations on the Annals, then failed at the Ministry of Rites; he was appointed Confucian instructor in Ningguo Circuit.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yanyou reign he passed the provincial examination in the Spring and Autumn Annals, went up to the Ministry of Rites, failed the metropolitan examination, and was appointed Instructor at the Confucian school of Ningguo Circuit.

value.zh: 五年，遂登進士第，授承事郎、同知岳州路平江州事。
value.en: Five years later he passed the jinshi examinations and was made gentleman for affairs and vice prefect of Pingjiang under Yuezhou Circuit.
value.literal: In the fifth year he attained the jinshi degree and was appointed Gentleman for Affairs and Vice Commissioner of the administrative affairs of Pingjiang Prefecture under Yuezhou Circuit.

value.zh: 以母年八十，上書願奪所授官一等或二等，得近地以便養，不允。
value.en: His mother being eighty, he petitioned to be demoted one or two ranks in exchange for a nearby post to care for her; the court refused.
value.literal: Because his mother was eighty, he submitted a memorial asking to be reduced one or two ranks from the office just granted so that he might receive a nearby post to support her; this was not approved.

value.zh: 南歸奉母之官。
value.en: He returned south and brought his mother to his office.
value.literal: He returned south and took her with him to his post.

value.zh: 州民李氏，以貲雄，其弟死，妻誓不他適，兄利其財，嗾族人誣婦以姦事。
value.en: A wealthy townsman surnamed Li had a brother who died; the widow swore she would not remarry, but the elder brother coveted her estate and goaded kinsmen to accuse her of adultery.
value.literal: A commoner of the prefecture surnamed Li, wealthy and overbearing, had a younger brother who died; the wife vowed not to marry another, but the elder brother coveted her property and incited clansmen to accuse the widow of adultery.

value.zh: 獄成而澤民至，察知其枉，為直之。
value.en: By the time the case was closed and Zemin arrived, he saw the injustice and reversed the verdict.
value.literal: The case had been concluded when Zemin arrived; perceiving the injustice, he set the matter right.

value.zh: 會朝廷徵江南包銀，府檄澤民分辨，民不擾而事​​集。
value.en: When the court imposed the bao-yin levy on Jiangnan, the prefecture put Zemin in charge of apportioning it; the people were not troubled and the collection was completed.
value.literal: Just then the court levied the bao-yin silver tax in Jiangnan; the prefecture ordered Zemin to apportion it, and the people were not disturbed while the task was completed.

value.zh: 尋遷南安路總管府推官。
value.en: He was soon promoted to reviewing official in the Nan'an chief administrator's office.
value.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Nan'an Circuit.

value.zh: 鎮守萬戶朵兒赤，持官府短長，郡吏王甲，毆傷屬縣長官，訴郡，同僚畏朵兒赤，托故不視事，澤民獨捕甲，系之獄。
value.en: The garrison commander Dorbet knew every weakness in the local administration. When a prefectural clerk named Wang Jia assaulted a county magistrate, colleagues feared Dorbet and declined the case; Zemin alone arrested Wang Jia and jailed him.
value.literal: The garrison commander Wanhu Dorbet, who knew the failings of the government offices, had a prefectural clerk Wang Jia who beat and injured a magistrate of a subordinate county; the case was brought to the prefecture, but colleagues feared Dorbet and excused themselves from hearing it; Zemin alone arrested Jia and imprisoned him.

value.zh: 朵兒赤賂巡按御史，受甲家人訴，欲出之，澤民正色與辨，御史沮怍，夜竟去，乃卒罪王甲。
value.en: Dorbet bribed the touring censor, who took the family's petition and tried to free Jia. Zemin argued him down face to face; the censor withdrew in shame that night, and Wang Jia was convicted at last.
value.literal: Dorbet bribed the touring surveillance censor, who accepted the petition from Jia's family and wished to release him; Zemin spoke sternly in argument, the censor was shamed and abashed and fled in the night, and Jia was finally punished.

value.zh: 潮州府判官錢珍，以姦淫事殺推官梁楫，事連廣東廉訪副使劉珍，坐系者二百餘人，省府官凡六委官鞫問，皆顧忌淹延弗能白，复檄澤民讞之，獄立具，人服其明。
value.en: Chaozhou's prefectural judge Qian Zhen murdered reviewing official Liang Ji in a scandal of adultery that implicated Guangdong's deputy surveillance commissioner Liu Zhen. More than two hundred people were held; six rounds of officials sent to investigate shrank back from the powerful interests involved. When Zemin was ordered to try the case, he concluded it at once, and all marveled at his discernment.
value.literal: Qian Zhen, prefectural judge of Chaozhou, had killed the reviewing official Liang Ji over an affair of debauchery; the case implicated Liu Zhen, deputy surveillance commissioner of Guangdong; more than two hundred persons were detained; six times provincial and circuit officials commissioned officers to interrogate, but all hesitated and delayed and could not clear the matter; again they ordered Zemin to report on the case, and the dossier was immediately complete—men admired his clarity.

value.zh: 遷信州路總管府推官。
value.en: He was transferred to reviewing official in the Xinzhou chief administrator's office.
value.literal: He was transferred to be Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Xinzhou Circuit.

value.zh: 丁母憂，服除，授平江路總管府推官。
value.en: After mourning his mother, he was appointed reviewing official in the Pingjiang chief administrator's office.
value.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Pingjiang Circuit.

value.zh: 有僧淨廣，與他僧有憾，久絕往來，一日，邀廣飲，廣弟子急欲得師財，且苦其棰楚，潛往它僧所殺之。
value.en: A monk named Jingguang had a feud with another monk and had long ceased visiting him. One day he invited Guang to drink. Guang's disciple, eager for his master's property and weary of his beatings, stole to the rival monk's quarters and killed him.
value.literal: There was a monk Jingguang who bore a grudge against another monk and had long ceased visiting him; one day he invited Guang to drink; Guang's disciple, eager to seize his master's property and weary of his beatings, secretly went to the other monk's place and killed him.

value.zh: 明日訴官，它僧不勝考掠，乃誣服，三經審錄，詞無異，結案等報。
value.en: The next day the crime was reported. The other monk broke under torture and confessed falsely. After three examinations his story never changed, and the case was closed pending execution.
value.literal: The next day the case was reported to the authorities; the other monk could not endure the torture and falsely confessed; through three rounds of examination the testimony did not change, and the case was closed awaiting execution.

value.zh: 澤民取行凶刀視之，刀上有鐵工姓名，召工問之，乃其弟子刀也，一訊吐實，即械之而出他僧，人驚以為神。
value.en: Zemin inspected the murder weapon and found an ironsmith's mark on the blade. The smith identified it as the disciple's knife. One interrogation brought out the truth; Zemin shackled the disciple and freed the other monk, and people called it uncanny.
value.literal: Zemin examined the murder weapon and found on the blade the name of the ironsmith; he summoned the smith and learned it was the disciple's knife; on one interrogation the truth came out, and he immediately shackled the disciple and released the other monk—people were astonished and called it divine.

value.zh: 調濟寧路兗州知州，孔子後衍聖公襲封職三品，澤民建議，以謂宜升其品秩，以示褒崇宣聖之意，廷議從之。
value.en: Transferred to prefect of Yanzhou in Jining Circuit, he proposed raising the hereditary third-rank title of Confucius's descendant the Yanshenggong to show the court's reverence for the Sage; the proposal was adopted.
value.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Yanzhou in Jining Circuit; the Yanshenggong, lineal descendant of Confucius, held a third-rank hereditary enfeoffment; Zemin proposed that his rank should be raised to show honor to the Sage, and the court deliberation approved.

value.zh: 武用妻蘇氏，真定人，徙家京師。
value.en: Wu Yong's wife, Lady Su, came from Zhending; the family later moved to the capital.
value.literal: Wu Yong's wife, Lady Su, was a person of Zhending; [her family] moved their residence to the capital.

value.zh: 用疾，蘇氏刲股為粥以進，疾即愈。
value.en: When Yong fell sick, Lady Su sliced flesh from her own thigh to prepare porridge for him, and he soon recovered.
value.literal: Yong fell ill; Lady Su cut flesh from her thigh to make gruel and presented it; the illness then immediately healed.

value.zh: 生子德政，四歲而寡。
value.en: She gave birth to a son named Dezheng and was widowed when the boy was four.
value.literal: She bore a son, Dezheng; when he was four she became a widow.

value.zh: 夫之兄利其資，欲逼而嫁之，不聽。
value.en: Her husband's older brother wanted her wealth and tried to pressure her into marrying again, but she refused.
value.literal: Her husband's elder brother coveted her property and wished to force her to remarry; she would not listen.

value.zh: 未幾夫兄舉家死，惟餘三弱孫，蘇氏取而育之。
value.en: Soon afterward her brother-in-law's entire family perished, leaving only three frail grandsons, whom Lady Su took in and reared.
value.literal: Before long the husband's brother's whole household died; only three weak grandsons remained; Lady Su took them and raised them.

value.zh: 德政長，事蘇氏至孝。
value.en: When Dezheng came of age, he treated Lady Su with the utmost devotion.
value.literal: Dezheng grew up and served Lady Su with utmost filial piety.

value.zh: 蘇氏死時，天大旱，德政方掘地求水以供葬事，忽二蛇躍出，德政因默禱焉。
value.en: Lady Su died during a severe drought. While Dezheng was digging for water for her funeral, two snakes suddenly sprang from the ground, and he prayed to them in silence.
value.literal: When Lady Su died, the sky was greatly drought-stricken; Dezheng was just digging the earth seeking water to supply the burial affairs; suddenly two serpents leaped out; Dezheng thereupon silently prayed.

value.zh: 二蛇一東一北，隨其地掘之，果得泉。
value.en: One snake went east and the other north; he dug where they led and found a spring.
value.literal: The two serpents, one [going] east and one north—following their directions in digging—indeed obtained a spring.

value.zh: 有司上其事。
value.en: The authorities reported the affair to the court.
value.literal: The officials reported this matter upward.

value.zh: 旌復其家。
value.en: The court honored the family and granted it tax relief.
value.literal: [They] commended and exempted her household [from corvée and taxes].

value.zh: 劉氏二女，長曰貞，年十九；
value.en: The Liu family had two daughters. The elder was named Zhen and was nineteen;
value.literal: The two daughters of the Liu family: the elder was named Zhen, age nineteen;

value.zh: 次曰孫，年十七。
value.en: the younger was named Sun and was seventeen.
value.literal: the younger was named Sun, age seventeen.

value.zh: 龍興人，皆未許嫁。
value.en: They were from Longxing, and neither had yet been betrothed.
value.literal: They were from Longxing; neither had yet been betrothed.

value.zh: 陳友諒寇龍興，其母泣謂二女曰：「城或破，置汝何所？」
value.en: When Chen Youliang attacked Longxing, their mother wept and asked the two girls, "If the city falls, where can I keep you safe?"
value.literal: Chen Youliang attacked Longxing; their mother weeping said to the two daughters, "If the city should fall, where shall I place you?"

value.zh: 二女曰：「寧死不辱父母也。」
value.en: The two daughters answered, "We would rather die than bring shame on our parents."
value.literal: The two daughters said, "Better to die than to disgrace our parents."

value.zh: 城陷，二女登樓，相繼自縊。
value.en: When the city fell, the two girls went up to a tower and hanged themselves, one after the other.
value.literal: When the city fell, the two daughters ascended a tower and hanged themselves one after the other.

value.zh: 婢鄭奴，亦自縊。
value.en: Their maid Zhengnu hanged herself as well.
value.literal: The maid Zhengnu also hanged herself.

value.zh: 漢紀五十九起閼逢敦牂，盡柔兆涒灘，凡三年。
value.en: Han Records 59 Spanning from the year Yanfeng Dunxiang through Rouzhao Toushan—a period of three years.
value.literal: Han Records 59 Beginning with Yanfeng Dunxiang, ending with Rouzhao Toushan, three years in all.

value.zh: 秋，七月，魏公操擊孫權，留少子臨菑侯植守鄴。
value.en: In autumn, during the seventh month, Duke Cao attacked Sun Quan and left his youngest son, Marquis of Linzi Cao Zhi, to guard Ye.
value.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Duke Cao attacked Sun Quan, leaving his youngest son Marquis of Linzi Zhi to guard Ye.

value.zh: 操為諸子高選官屬，以刑顒為植家丞。
value.en: Cao carefully chose staff for his sons and made Xing Yong household aide to Zhi.
value.literal: Cao for his sons carefully selected staff, making Xing Yong Zhi's household aide.

value.zh: 顒防閒以禮，無所屈撓，由是不合。
value.en: Yong kept him in check with strict ritual propriety and would not bend, and for that reason they did not get along.
value.literal: Yong guarded and restrained him with ritual propriety, yielding in nothing, and for this reason they did not get along.

value.zh: 庶子劉楨美文辭，植親愛之。
value.en: Liu Zhen, a junior associate, wrote fine prose, and Zhi was fond of him.
value.literal: Associate Liu Zhen had fine literary style; Zhi was fond of him.

value.zh: 楨以書諫植曰：「君侯采庶子之春華，忘家丞之秋實，為上招謗，其罪不小，愚實懼焉。」
value.en: Zhen wrote to admonish Zhi, "You gather the spring blossoms your junior offers but forget the autumn fruit your household aide provides. You invite your father's reproach, and the fault is no small one. I am truly afraid for you."
value.literal: Zhen admonished Zhi in a letter: "Your Lordship gathers the associate's spring flowers but forgets the household aide's autumn fruit—this invites slander from above, and the fault is no small one; I truly fear it."

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第094卷
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 94
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 94

value.zh: 曜見勒，曰：「石王，頗憶重門之盟否？」
value.en: When Liu Yao was brought before Shi Le, he said: "King Shi, do you still remember our pact at Chongmen?"
value.literal: When Yao saw Le he said: "King Shi, do you still recall the covenant at Chongmen?"

value.zh: 勒使徐光謂之曰：「今日之事，天使其然，復雲何邪！」
value.en: Shi Le had Xu Guang reply: "What has happened today Heaven itself ordained—what more is there to say!"
value.literal: Le had Xu Guang tell him: "Today's matter Heaven has made so—what further can one say!"

value.zh: 乙酉，勒班師。
value.en: On yiyou, Shi Le withdrew his army.
value.literal: On yiyou, Le withdrew the army.

value.zh: 使征東將軍石邃將兵衛送曜。
value.en: He sent Eastern Campaign General Shi Sui with troops to guard and escort Liu Yao.
value.literal: He sent Eastern Campaign General Shi Sui to lead troops guarding and escorting Yao.

value.zh: 邃，虎之子也。
value.en: Shi Sui was Shi Hu's son.
value.literal: Sui was Hu's son.

value.zh: 曜瘡甚，載以馬輿，使醫李永與同載。
value.en: Liu Yao's wounds were grave. He was carried in a horse-drawn litter, with the physician Li Yong riding beside him.
value.literal: Yao's wounds were severe; he was carried in a horse litter with the physician Li Yong riding with him.

value.zh: 己亥，至襄國，捨曜於永豐小城，給其妓妾，嚴兵圍守。
value.en: On jihai they reached Xiangguo. Liu Yao was housed in the small town of Yongfeng, given singing girls and concubines, and kept under heavy guard.
value.literal: On jihai they reached Xiangguo; they lodged Yao in Yongfeng small town, supplied him with courtesans, and surrounded him with strict troops.

value.zh: 遣劉岳、劉震等從男女盛服以見之，曜曰：「吾謂卿等久為灰土，石王仁厚，乃全宥至今邪！
value.en: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen, and others, followed by men and women in fine dress, to visit him. Liu Yao said: "I thought you had long since turned to dust. King Shi is generous indeed—to have spared you all until now!
value.literal: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen, and others followed by men and women in splendid dress to see him; Yao said: "I thought you had long been ashes; King Shi's kindness and generosity—yet he fully spared you till now!

value.zh: 我殺石佗，愧之多矣。
value.en: When I killed Shi Tuo, I already owed him more shame than I can count.
value.literal: I killed Shi Tuo—a weight of shame.

value.zh: 今日之禍，自其分耳。」
value.en: The disaster that has befallen me today is simply my allotted fate."
value.literal: Today's calamity is simply what was fated."

value.zh: 留宴終日而去。
value.en: They remained and feasted with him all day before departing.
value.literal: They stayed feasting all day then left.

value.zh: 勒使曜與其太子熙書，諭令速降；
value.en: Shi Le had Liu Yao write to his crown prince Liu Xi, urging him to surrender quickly;
value.literal: Le had Yao write to his crown prince Xi, instructing swift surrender;

value.zh: 曜但敕熙與諸大臣「匡維社稷，勿以吾易意也。」
value.en: but Liu Yao merely instructed Xi and the chief ministers: "Hold firm to the altars of state. Do not alter your purpose because of me."
value.literal: But Yao only ordered Xi and the ministers "Uphold the altars of state; do not change your resolve on my account."

value.zh: 勒見而惡之，久之，乃殺曜。
value.en: When Shi Le read the letter he was disgusted, and after some time he had Liu Yao executed.
value.literal: Le saw it and loathed it; after some time he killed Yao.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第241卷
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 241
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 241

value.zh: 自元和之末，宦官益橫，建置天子在其掌握，威權出人主之右，人莫敢言。
value.en: Since the close of the Yuanhe era the eunuchs had grown ever bolder, enthroning and deposing emperors at will. Their power eclipsed the throne itself, and no one dared protest.
value.literal: From the end of the Yuanhe era the eunuchs grew ever more overbearing; they installed and removed emperors at their grasp, and their authority and power stood to the right of the sovereign—no one dared speak.

value.zh: 辛已，上親策制舉人，賢良方正，昌平劉蕡對策極言其禍，其略曰：「陛下宜先憂者：宮闈將變，社稷將危，天下將傾，海內將亂。」
value.en: On the xinsi day the emperor held the special civil examination for "upright and good" candidates. Liu Zhen of Changping answered with a memorial that laid bare the peril in the plainest terms: "Your Majesty's first concerns ought to be these: the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval, the altars of state are in danger, the realm is tottering, and turmoil is about to engulf the empire."
value.literal: On the day xinsi the emperor personally examined the civil-service candidates of the special decree examination for "upright and good," and Liu Zhen of Changping answered the policy question by speaking bluntly of the disaster; in summary he said: "What Your Majesty should worry about first: the inner palace is about to change, the altars of state are about to be endangered, the realm is about to topple, and within the seas disorder is about to break out."

value.zh: 又曰：「陛下將杜篡弒之漸，則居正位而近正人，遠刀鋸之賤，親骨鯁之直，輔相得以專其任，庶職得以守其官，奈何以褻近五六人總天下大政！
value.en: He went on: "To choke off the drift toward regicide, hold the throne in dignity and keep honest men close. Banish the butcher's minions; cherish the blunt counselors who speak truth. Let your chief ministers govern, and let every office do its work—how can five or six favored eunuchs run the empire?
value.literal: He also said: "If Your Majesty wishes to cut off the gradual growth of usurpation and regicide, then occupy the correct position and keep upright men near, keep far from the base of the knife and saw, be close to blunt, loyal remonstrators, let the chief ministers fully carry out their duties, and let the hundred offices keep to their posts—how can you let five or six lewd intimates hold all great government of the realm!

value.zh: 禍稔蕭牆，奸生帷幄，臣恐曹節、侯覽復生於今日。」
value.en: Disaster is ripening behind the palace walls; treachery is breeding within the curtained hall. I fear that Cao Jie and Hou Lan live again in our time."
value.literal: Disaster ripens within the palace walls; treachery is born inside the curtain. I fear Cao Jie and Hou Lan are being reborn in our own day."

value.zh: 又曰：「忠賢無腹心之寄，閫寺恃廢立之權，陷先君不得正其終，致陛下不得正其始。」
value.en: He also wrote: "Loyal ministers have nowhere to place their trust. The eunuch commanders rest on the power to make and unmake emperors. They prevented your predecessor from ending his reign in peace, and they have kept you from beginning yours in legitimacy."
value.literal: He also said: "Loyal ministers have no place to lodge their hearts; the eunuch commanders rely on the power to depose and establish [emperors]. They trapped the late emperor so that he could not end his reign properly, and they have caused Your Majesty not to begin yours properly."

value.zh: 又曰：「威柄陵夷，籓臣跋扈。
value.en: He also said: "Sovereign power erodes daily, while the military commissioners grow insolent on their borders.
value.literal: He also said: "Imperial authority declines day by day; the frontier lords are arrogant and domineering.

value.zh: 或有不達人臣之節，首亂者以安君為名；
value.en: Some who lack a subject's restraint raise rebellion in the name of saving the throne;
value.literal: Some who do not understand a subject's propriety take the lead in disorder in the name of securing the ruler;

value.zh: 不究《春秋》之微，稱兵者以逐惡為義。
value.en: without grasping the Spring and Autumn Annals' deeper lesson, men who march armies call it righteous to expel the wicked.
value.literal: without probing the subtle meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, those who take up arms claim the righteousness of driving out evil.

value.zh: 則政刑不由乎天子，征伐必自於諸侯。」
value.en: Then law and punishment no longer flow from the Son of Heaven, and war is waged only at the command of the regional lords."
value.literal: Then government and punishments no longer proceed from the Son of Heaven, and campaigns and punishments necessarily originate with the feudal lords."

value.zh: 又曰：「陛下何不塞陰邪之路，屏褻狎之臣，制侵陵迫脅之心，復門戶掃除之役，戒其所宜戒，憂其所宜憂！
value.en: He urged: "Block the road of secret malice. Cast out the emperor's coarse intimates. Curb the impulse to bully and threaten. Restore the old duties of gatekeeping and court order. Warn yourself where warning is needed; fear what ought to be feared.
value.literal: He also said: "Why does Your Majesty not block the path of hidden evil, dismiss lewd and familiar ministers, restrain hearts that encroach and coerce, restore the work of guarding the gates and sweeping the court—warn where warning is due, and worry where worry is due!

value.zh: 既不能治於前，當治於後，既不能正其始，當正其終；
value.en: If you could not set things right at the start, set them right at the finish; if you could not cure what came before, cure what comes after.
value.literal: If you could not govern what came before, govern what comes after; if you could not set right the beginning, set right the end;

value.zh: 則可以虔奉典謨，克承丕構矣。
value.en: Then you may reverently uphold the classics and inherit the great enterprise of your house.
value.literal: then you may reverently follow the canonical models and succeed to the great foundation.

value.zh: 昔秦之亡也失於強暴，漢之亡也失於微弱。
value.en: Qin fell because its rule was too brutal; Han fell because its rule was too feeble.
value.literal: In antiquity Qin perished through excess violence; Han perished through excess weakness.

value.zh: 強暴則賊臣畏死而害上，微弱則奸臣竊權而震主。
value.en: Under brutal rule, treacherous ministers, fearing for their lives, murder their lord; under feeble rule, crafty ministers seize power and terrify the throne.
value.literal: When violent, treacherous ministers fear death and harm their sovereign; when weak, crafty ministers steal power and shake the throne.

value.zh: 伏見敬宗皇帝不虞亡秦之禍，不翦其萌。
value.en: I see that Emperor Jingzong never foresaw Qin's fate and never cut the evil in its bud.
value.literal: I observe that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's manner of perishing and did not cut off the evil at its sprout.

value.zh: 伏惟陛下深軫亡漢之憂，以杜其漸，則祖宗之鴻業可紹，三、五之遐軌可追矣。」
value.en: I pray that Your Majesty will take Han's fall deeply to heart and stop the rot while it is still slight. Then the ancestral legacy may be renewed and the distant example of the sage kings pursued once more."
value.literal: I pray that Your Majesty will deeply take to heart Han's manner of perishing and cut off the gradual growth of evil; then the magnificent enterprise of the ancestors may be continued, and the distant model of the Three Dynasties may be pursued."

value.zh: 又曰：「臣聞昔漢元帝即位之初，更制七十餘事，其心甚誠，其稱甚美，然而紀綱日紊，國祚日衰，奸宄日強，黎元日困者，以其不能擇賢明而任之，失其操柄也。」
value.en: He also wrote: "When Emperor Yuan of Han first reigned he reformed more than seventy institutions. His intent was sincere and his praise resounded—yet order unraveled daily, the dynasty weakened daily, villains grew bolder daily, and the people suffered daily, because he could not choose wise men and give them real authority. He lost the tiller of state."
value.literal: He also said: "I have heard that when Emperor Yuan of Han first took the throne he changed more than seventy institutions; his heart was very sincere and his reputation very fine—yet day by day the statutes grew disorderly, day by day the fortune of the state declined, day by day treachery grew strong, and day by day the common people were distressed, because he could not choose the worthy and enlightened and employ them, and lost hold of the helm."

value.zh: 又曰：「陛下誠能揭國權以歸相，持兵柄以歸將，則心無不達，行無不孚矣。」
value.en: He said further: "If Your Majesty will truly restore civil authority to the chief ministers and military authority to the generals, nothing you intend will go unheard and nothing you do will lack credibility."
value.literal: He also said: "If Your Majesty can truly raise the authority of the state and return it to the chief ministers, and hold the military power and return it to the generals, then no thought will go unheeded and no act will fail to win trust."

value.zh: 又曰：「法宜畫一，官宜正名。
value.en: He also said: "Law should be one; offices should bear their proper names.
value.literal: He also said: "The law ought to be uniform; offices ought to have correct names.

value.zh: 今分外官、中官之員，立南司、北司之局，或犯禁於南則亡命於北，或正刑於外則破律於中，法出多門，人無所措，實由兵農勢異而中外法殊也。」
value.en: Today outer and inner officials multiply without limit; southern and northern bureaus stand side by side. Break the law in one jurisdiction and flee to the other; punish a crime in the open court and see it voided within the palace. When law has many mouths, the people do not know where to stand. This comes of treating army and empire as separate worlds, with one law for the court and another for the realm."
value.literal: Now the posts of outer officials and inner officials are set up separately, and the bureaus of the southern and northern administrations are established; if one violates prohibition in the south he flees to the north, if one is punished by regular law outside he breaks the statutes within—law issues from many gates and people have nowhere to turn; this truly comes from the differing power of soldiers and farmers and the differing law inside and outside."

value.zh: 又曰：「今夏官不知兵籍，止於奉朝請；
value.en: "He went on: Today the Ministry of War no longer knows the rolls of the armies and exists only to attend morning audience;
value.literal: "He also said: "This summer the Ministry of War does not know the military registers and is limited to attendance at court;"

value.zh: 六軍不主兵事，止於養勳階。
value.en: The Six Armies no longer commanded military affairs but only cultivated ranks of merit.
value.literal: The Six Armies do not command military affairs but only cultivate ranks of merit.

value.zh: 軍容合中官之政，戎律附內臣之職。
value.en: Military prestige merged with eunuch policy, and martial law became an inner-court function.
value.literal: Military prestige merged with the policies of inner officials; martial law attached to the duties of palace servants.

value.zh: 首一戴武弁，疾文吏如仇讎。
value.en: Once they donned the warrior's cap, they hated civil officials like mortal enemies.
value.literal: Once they donned the warrior's cap, they hated civil officials like mortal enemies.

value.zh: 足一蹈軍門，視農夫如草芥。
value.en: Once they entered the army gate, they treated farmers as worthless weeds.
value.literal: Once they set foot in the army gate, they regarded farmers as worthless weeds.

value.zh: 謀不足以翦除凶逆，而詐足以抑揚威福；
value.en: They lacked the wit to destroy traitors, yet their cunning sufficed to raise and lower power and favor;
value.literal: Their plotting was insufficient to cut down the vicious and rebellious, yet their deceit was enough to raise and lower power and favor;

value.zh: 勇不足以鎮衛社稷，而暴足以侵軼里閭。
value.en: their courage could not guard the realm, yet their violence could trample villages and lanes.
value.literal: their courage was insufficient to guard the altars of state, yet their violence was enough to trample villages and lanes.

value.zh: 羈紲籓臣，干陵宰舖，隳裂王度，汩亂朝經。
value.en: They bound frontier ministers, overawed chief ministers, shattered royal standards, and muddied court regulations.
value.literal: They bound frontier ministers, overawed chief ministers, shattered royal standards, and muddied court regulations.

value.zh: 張武夫之威，上以制君父；
value.en: They stretched warriors' might upward to control emperor and father;
value.literal: They stretched the might of warriors upward to control father and sovereign;

value.zh: 假天子之命，下以御英豪。
value.en: they borrowed the Son of Heaven's mandate downward to command heroes and champions.
value.literal: they borrowed the Son of Heaven's mandate downward to command heroes and champions.

value.zh: 有藏奸觀釁之父，無伏節死難之義。
value.en: There were fathers who hid treachery and watched for openings, but none who died loyal deaths for the throne.
value.literal: There were fathers who hid treachery and watched for openings, but no righteousness of laying down one's life in loyal death.

value.zh: 豈先王經文緯武之旨邪！」
value.en: How could this be what the former kings intended when they wove culture and arms together!"
value.literal: How could this be the intent of the former kings who wove culture and martial power together!"

value.zh: 又曰：「臣非不知言發而禍應，計行而身戮，蓋痛社稷之危，哀生人之困，豈忍姑息時忌，竊陛下一命之寵哉！」
value.en: He also wrote, 'I know that words bring calamity and action brings death — yet I grieve the realm's peril and pity the people's distress. How could I indulge the taboos of the age and steal Your Majesty's favor!'
value.literal: He also said: 'Your servant is not unaware that words once spoken bring calamity in answer, and plans once carried out bring the body to execution — yet I grieve the altars of state in peril and pity the people's distress; how could I bear to indulge the taboos of the time and steal Your Majesty's single favor of office!'

value.zh: 資治通鑑第248卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 248
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 248

value.zh: 劉稹腹心將高文端降，言賊中乏食，令婦人挼穗舂之以給軍。
value.en: Gao Wenduan, a trusted Liu Zhen commander, defected and reported that the rebels were short of food and had women thresh grain by hand to feed the troops.
value.literal: Liu Zhen's trusted general Gao Wenduan surrendered, saying that within the rebel ranks food was scarce and they had women rub ears of grain and pound them to supply the army.

value.zh: 德裕訪文端破賊之策，文端以為：「官軍今真攻澤州，恐多殺士卒，城未易得。
value.en: Deyu asked Wenduan how to break the rebels. Wenduan said: "If our army assaults Ze Prefecture head-on, we will lose many men and still may not take the city.
value.literal: Deyu asked Wenduan for a strategy to defeat the rebels; Wenduan held that: "If government troops now truly attack Ze Prefecture, I fear many soldiers will be killed and the city will not be easily taken.

value.zh: 澤州兵約萬五千人，賊常分兵太半，潛伏山谷，伺官軍攻城疲弊，則四集救之，官軍必失利。
value.en: Ze holds about fifteen thousand men. The rebels habitually keep more than half their force hidden in the hills, waiting until our siege troops are exhausted, then converge from every direction—the assault will fail.
value.literal: Ze Prefecture has about fifteen thousand troops; the rebels often divide more than half their forces, lie hidden in valleys, wait until government troops are worn out from attacking the city, then gather from four sides to rescue it, and government troops will certainly suffer defeat.

value.zh: 今請令陳許軍過乾河立寨，自寨城連延築為夾城，環繞澤州，日遣大軍布陳於外以扞救兵。
value.en: Instead, have the Chenxu army cross the Gan River and build a camp, then extend linked walls in a double enclosure all around Ze. Each day station a large force outside to block relief columns.
value.literal: Now I ask that the Chenxu army be ordered to cross the Gan River and establish a camp, and from the camp city continuously build a twin-walled encirclement ringing Ze Prefecture, daily sending large forces to deploy formations outside to ward off relief troops.

value.zh: 賊見圍城將合，必出大戰；
value.en: Seeing the ring about to close, the rebels will surely sally out for a decisive fight;
value.literal: When the rebels see the siege walls about to close, they will certainly come out for a great battle;

value.zh: 待其敗北，然後乘勢可取。」
value.en: once they are beaten and retreating, we can take the city at a stroke."
value.literal: wait until they are defeated and flee north, then ride the momentum and they can be taken."

value.zh: 德裕奏請詔示王宰。
value.en: Deyu memorialized that this plan be sent to Wang Zai by imperial order.
value.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict be issued to inform Wang Zai.

value.zh: 文端又言：「固鎮寨四崖懸絕，勢不可攻。
value.en: Wenduan added: "The Guzhen stockade sits on sheer cliffs on all four sides and cannot be stormed.
value.literal: Wenduan also said: "The Guzhen camp's four cliffs hang sheer; by its terrain it cannot be attacked.

value.zh: 然寨中無水，皆飲澗水，在寨東南約一里許。
value.en: But the camp has no water of its own; everyone drinks from a stream about a li to the southeast.
value.literal: Yet within the camp there is no water; all drink stream water about one li southeast of the camp.

value.zh: 宜令王逢進兵逼之，絕其水道，不過三日，賊必棄寨遁去，官軍即可追躡。
value.en: Have Wang Feng advance and seize the stream. Within three days the rebels will abandon the camp; our troops can then run them down.
value.literal: It is fitting to order Wang Feng to advance troops and press them, cut off their water route—in no more than three days the rebels will surely abandon the camp and flee, and government troops can immediately pursue.

value.zh: 前十五里至青龍寨，亦四崖懸絕，水在寨外，可以前法取也。
value.en: Fifteen li farther on lies Qinglong Camp, equally cliff-bound with its water outside—the same method will work there.
value.literal: Fifteen li ahead is Qinglong Camp, likewise with four sheer cliffs; water is outside the camp, and the previous method can be used to take it.

value.zh: 其東十五里則沁州城。」
value.en: Fifteen li east of that stands Qin Prefecture city."
value.literal: Fifteen li east of that is Qin Prefecture city."

value.zh: 德裕奏請詔示王逢。
value.en: Deyu memorialized that these instructions be sent to Wang Feng by imperial order.
value.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict be issued to inform Wang Feng.

value.zh: 文端又言：「都頭王釗將萬兵戍洺州，劉稹既族薛茂卿，又誅刑洺救援兵馬使談朝義兄弟三人，釗自是疑懼。
value.en: Wenduan also said: "Commander Wang Zhao holds Ming Prefecture with ten thousand men. Liu Zhen had already wiped out the Xue Maqing clan and executed Tan Chaoyi, the Ming relief commander, together with his three brothers. Zhao has been fearful and suspicious ever since.
value.literal: Wenduan also said: "Commander Wang Zhao leads ten thousand troops garrisoning Ming Prefecture. After Liu Zhen had the Xue Maqing clan executed and also put to death the Ming relief army commander Tan Chaoyi and his three brothers, Zhao from that time was suspicious and afraid.

value.zh: 稹遣使召之，釗不肯入，士卒皆嘩噪，釗必不為稹用。
value.en: Zhen sent to summon him, but Zhao would not come in; his troops are in an uproar. He will not fight for Zhen.
value.literal: Zhen sent envoys to summon him; Zhao refused to enter, the soldiers all clamored, and Zhao will certainly not serve Zhen.

value.zh: 但釗及士卒家屬皆在潞州，又士卒恐己降為官軍所殺，招之必不肯來。
value.en: Yet Zhao's and his men's families are all in Lu Prefecture, and the troops fear that surrender means execution. They will not come if we merely call.
value.literal: But Zhao and the soldiers' families are all in Lu Prefecture, and moreover the soldiers fear that if they surrender they will be killed by government troops; if summoned they will certainly not come.

value.zh: 惟有諭意於釗，使引兵入潞州取稹。
value.en: We should instead make our terms clear to Zhao: lead your men into Lu Prefecture and seize Liu Zhen.
value.literal: Only by conveying our intent to Zhao, making him lead troops into Lu Prefecture to seize Zhen.

value.zh: 事成之日，許除別道節度使，仍厚有賜與，庶幾肯從。」
value.en: Promise him a military governorship on another circuit and rich rewards when he succeeds—then he may agree."
value.literal: On the day the affair succeeds, promise to appoint him military governor of another circuit and still give generous rewards—then perhaps he will consent."

value.zh: 德裕奏請詔何弘潛遣人諭以此意。
value.en: Deyu memorialized that He Hongjing be ordered by edict to send an envoy with this proposal.
value.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict order He Hongjing to send someone to explain this intent.

value.zh: 劉稹年少懦弱，押牙王協、宅內兵馬使李士貴用事，專聚貨財，府庫充溢，而將士有功無賞，由是人心離怨。
value.en: Liu Zhen was young and timid. Wang Xie, his yamen guard, and Li Shigui, commander of the household troops, ran affairs, hoarding wealth until the vaults brimmed while meritorious officers went unrewarded. Disaffection spread through the ranks.
value.literal: Liu Zhen was young and weak; the yamen guard Wang Xie and the household army commander Li Shigui held power, devoted solely to amassing wealth until the treasuries overflowed, while officers and soldiers who had merit received no reward—thereby hearts turned away in resentment.

value.zh: 劉從諫妻裴氏，冕之支孫也，憂稹將敗，其弟問典兵在山東，欲召之使掌軍政。
value.en: Lady Pei, Liu Congjian's widow and a collateral descendant of Pei Mian, feared Zhen's fall. Her younger brother Wen commanded troops in Shandong; she wanted to recall him to take charge of the army.
value.literal: Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was a collateral descendant of Pei Mian; fearing Zhen would be defeated, she wished to summon her younger brother Wen, who commanded troops in Shandong, to make him manage military affairs.

value.zh: 士貴恐問至奪己權，且洩其奸狀，乃曰：「山東之事仰成於五舅，若召之，是無三州也。」
value.en: Shigui feared Wen would displace him and expose his corruption. He said: "Shandong has been entrusted to the Fifth Uncle; recall him and we lose the three prefectures."
value.literal: Shigui feared that if Wen arrived he would seize his authority and also expose his wicked conduct, so he said: "Shandong affairs rely on completion by the Fifth Uncle; if he is summoned, that means losing the three prefectures."

value.zh: 乃上。
value.en: He then withdrew.
value.literal: He then went up.

value.zh: 王協薦王釗為洺州都知兵馬使。
value.en: Wang Xie recommended Wang Zhao as overall commander of Ming Prefecture's forces.
value.literal: Wang Xie recommended Wang Zhao as Ming Prefecture commander of military affairs.

value.zh: 釗得眾心，而多不遵使府約束，同列高元武、安玉言其有貳心。
value.en: Zhao won the soldiers' loyalty but often ignored headquarters orders. His peers Gao Yuanwu and An Yu accused him of disloyalty.
value.literal: Zhao won the troops' hearts, yet often did not follow the headquarters' regulations; his colleagues Gao Yuanwu and An Yu said he had a divided heart.

value.zh: 稹召之，釗辭以「到洺州未立少功，實所慚恨，乞留數月，然後詣府。」
value.en: Zhen summoned him. Zhao pleaded: "I have done little since reaching Ming and am ashamed to face headquarters. Grant me a few more months, then I will come in."
value.literal: Zhen summoned him; Zhao declined on the grounds that "since arriving at Ming Prefecture I have achieved little merit—this is truly my shame and regret; I beg to remain several months and then come to headquarters."

value.zh: 許之，王協請稅商人，每州遣軍將一人主之，名為稅商，實籍編戶家貲，至於什器無所遺，皆估為絹匹，十分取其二，率高其估。
value.en: Zhen agreed. Wang Xie proposed a merchant tax: each prefecture would send an officer to levy it. In practice they inventoried every registered household's assets down to household goods, appraised everything in silk bolts, and took two-tenths—always at inflated valuations.
value.literal: Permission was granted. Wang Xie requested to tax merchants: each prefecture would send one army officer to supervise it, called "merchant tax," but in fact they registered registered households' property; even utensils were not omitted—all were appraised as silk bolts, two-tenths taken, and the appraisals were usually set high.

value.zh: 民竭浮財及糗糧輸之，不能充，皆璟璟不安。
value.en: People drained their movable property and grain stores and still could not meet the demand; everywhere there was unrest and fear.
value.literal: The people exhausted floating wealth and dry provisions to pay it yet could not fill the quota; all were anxious and uneasy.

value.zh: 軍將劉溪尤貪殘，劉從諫棄不用。
value.en: The officer Liu Xi was notoriously rapacious; Liu Congjian had long refused to employ him.
value.literal: The army officer Liu Xi was especially greedy and cruel; Liu Congjian had cast him aside and not used him.

value.zh: 溪厚賂王協，協以刑州富商最多，命溪主之。
value.en: Xi bribed Wang Xie heavily. Xie assigned him Xing Prefecture, where the richest merchants were concentrated.
value.literal: Xi gave Wang Xie heavy bribes; Xie, because Xing Prefecture had the most wealthy merchants, ordered Xi to supervise it.

value.zh: 裴問所將兵號「夜飛」，多富商子弟，溪至，悉拘其父兄。
value.en: Pei Wen's unit, the "Night Flight," was largely drawn from merchant families. When Xi arrived he seized their fathers and elder brothers.
value.literal: The troops Pei Wen commanded were called "Night Flight," mostly sons of wealthy merchants; when Xi arrived he detained all their fathers and elder brothers.

value.zh: 軍士訴於問，問為之請，溪不許，以不遜語答之。
value.en: The soldiers appealed to Wen, who interceded for them. Xi refused and answered with insults.
value.literal: The soldiers appealed to Wen; Wen pleaded for them, but Xi would not agree and answered with insolent words.

value.zh: 問怒，密與麾下謀殺溪歸國，並告刺史崔嘏，嘏從之。
value.en: Wen, furious, secretly plotted with his men to kill Xi and submit to the court. He told Prefect Cui Gu, who agreed.
value.literal: Wen was enraged, secretly plotted with his subordinates to kill Xi and return to allegiance with the state, and also informed Prefect Cui Gu, who agreed.

value.zh: 丙子，嘏、問閉城，斬城中大將四人，請降於王元逵。
value.en: On the day bingzi, Gu and Wen shut the gates, executed four senior officers in the city, and offered surrender to Wang Yuankui.
value.literal: On the day bingzi, Gu and Wen closed the city, beheaded four great generals in the city, and requested surrender to Wang Yuankui.

value.zh: 時高元武在黨山，聞之，亦降。
value.en: Gao Yuanwu, then at Dang Mountain, heard the news and surrendered as well.
value.literal: At that time Gao Yuanwu was at Dang Mountain; on hearing this, he also surrendered.

value.zh: 先是使府賜洺州軍士布，人一端，尋有帖以折冬賜。
value.en: Headquarters had earlier given each Ming soldier a bolt of cloth, and a notice soon followed promising a mid-winter bonus.
value.literal: Earlier the headquarters had granted Ming Prefecture soldiers cloth, one bolt per man; soon there was a notice for a mid-winter grant.

value.zh: 會稅商軍將至洺州，王釗因人不安，謂軍士曰：「留後年少，政非己出。
value.en: As the tax officer was about to reach Ming, Zhao, sensing the troops' unrest, told them: "The young commissioner does not truly rule.
value.literal: Just as the merchant-tax army officer was about to reach Ming Prefecture, Wang Zhao, because the people were uneasy, said to the soldiers: "The acting commissioner is young; government is not his own.

value.zh: 今倉庫充實，足支十年，豈可不少散之以慰勞苦之士！
value.en: The warehouses are full enough for ten years. Should we not open them a little to reward men who have suffered?
value.literal: Now the storehouses are full, enough to last ten years—how can we not distribute a little to comfort the toiling soldiers!

value.zh: 使貼不可用也。」
value.en: Ignore headquarters' notice."
value.literal: The headquarters notice cannot be used."

value.zh: 乃擅開倉庫，給士卒人絹一匹，谷十二石，士卒大喜。
value.en: He opened the stores on his own authority and gave each man a bolt of silk and twelve piculs of grain. The troops were overjoyed.
value.literal: He then on his own authority opened the storehouses and gave each soldier one bolt of silk and twelve piculs of grain; the soldiers were greatly pleased.

value.zh: 釗遂閉城請降於何弘敬。
value.en: Zhao then shut the gates and offered surrender to He Hongjing.
value.literal: Zhao then closed the city and requested surrender to He Hongjing.

value.zh: 安玉在磁州，聞二州降，亦降於弘敬。
value.en: An Yu at Ci Prefecture, hearing that both prefectures had submitted, surrendered to Hongjing as well.
value.literal: An Yu was at Ci Prefecture; on hearing that the two prefectures had surrendered, he also surrendered to Hongjing.

value.zh: 堯山都知失馬使魏元談等降於王元逵，元逵以其久不下，皆殺之。
value.en: Wei Yuantan, commander at Yaoshan, and others surrendered to Wang Yuankui, who executed them all for having held out so long.
value.literal: The Yaoshan commander Wei Yuantan and others surrendered to Wang Yuankui; Yuankui, because they had long not submitted, killed them all.

value.zh: 八月，辛卯，鎮、魏奏邢、洺、磁三州降，宰相入賀。
value.en: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, the Zhen and Wei armies reported the surrender of Xing, Ming, and Ci. The chief ministers came in to offer congratulations.
value.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, Zhen and Wei reported that Xing, Ming, and Ci—the three prefectures—had surrendered; the chief ministers entered to congratulate.

value.zh: 李德裕曰：「昭義根本盡在山東，三州降，則上黨不日有變矣。」
value.en: Li Deyu said: "Zhaoyi's strength lay entirely in Shandong. With those three prefectures gone, Shangdang will collapse before long."
value.literal: Li Deyu said: "Zhaoyi's foundation is entirely in Shandong; with the three prefectures surrendered, Shangdang will before long have change."

value.zh: 上曰：「郭誼必梟劉稹以自贖。」
value.en: The Emperor said: "Guo Yi is sure to deliver Liu Zhen's head to save his own skin."
value.literal: The Emperor said: "Guo Yi will certainly present Liu Zhen's head to redeem himself."

value.zh: 德裕曰：「誠如聖料。」
value.en: Deyu said: "Your Majesty reads the situation exactly right."
value.literal: Deyu said: "It is truly as Your Sagely foresight judged."

value.zh: 上曰：「於今所宜先處者何事？」
value.en: The Emperor asked: "What should we settle first, now?"
value.literal: The Emperor said: "Of what should be handled first at present?"

value.zh: 德裕請以給事中盧弘止為三州留後，曰：「萬一鎮、魏請占三州，朝廷難於可否。」
value.en: Deyu proposed appointing Supervising Secretary Lu Hongzhi regent of the three prefectures. "If Zhen and Wei ask to keep them," he said, "the court will be hard pressed to refuse yet should not concede."
value.literal: Deyu requested that Supervising Secretary Lu Hongzhi be made regent of the three prefectures, saying: "In the event Zhen and Wei request to occupy the three prefectures, the court will find it hard to grant or refuse."

value.zh: 上從之。
value.en: The Emperor agreed.
value.literal: The Emperor followed this.

value.zh: 詔山南東道兼昭義節度使盧鈞乘驛赴鎮。
value.en: An edict ordered Lu Jun—governor of Shannan East who also held Zhaoyi—to hurry to his command by post relay.
value.literal: An edict ordered Lu Jun, military governor of Shannan East Circuit who also held Zhaoyi, to ride post-horses and proceed to his post.

value.zh: 潞人聞三州降，大懼。
value.en: When Lu Prefecture heard that the three prefectures had fallen, panic spread.
value.literal: The people of Lu heard the three prefectures had surrendered and were greatly afraid.

value.zh: 郭誼、王協謀殺劉稹以自贖，稹再從兄中軍使匡周兼押牙，誼患之，言於稹曰：「十三郎在牙院，諸將皆莫敢言事，恐為十三郎所疑而獲罪，以此失山東。
value.en: Guo Yi and Wang Xie plotted to kill Liu Zhen and save themselves. Zhen's cousin Kuang Zhou commanded the central army and also held the yamen guard; Yi feared him. He told Zhen: "With the Thirteenth Son in the headquarters courtyard, no general dares speak freely—we lost Shandong because of it.
value.literal: Guo Yi and Wang Xie plotted to kill Liu Zhen to redeem themselves; Zhen's second cousin once removed, the central army commander Kuang Zhou who also held the yamen guard, was a worry to Yi, who said to Zhen: "The Thirteenth Son is in the yamen courtyard; the generals all dare not speak on affairs, fearing the Thirteenth Son's suspicion and punishment—thereby we lost Shandong.

value.zh: 今誠得十三郎不入，則諸將始敢盡言，采於眾人，必獲長策。」
value.en: Keep him out, and the officers will finally speak plainly. Take counsel from all sides and we are sure to find a way forward."
value.literal: Now if we can truly keep the Thirteenth Son from entering, then the generals will begin to dare speak fully; gathering from the multitude, we will certainly obtain a long-term plan."

value.zh: 稹召匡周諭之，使稱疾不入。
value.en: Zhen summoned Kuang Zhou and told him to stay away on grounds of illness.
value.literal: Zhen summoned Kuang Zhou and instructed him to plead illness and not enter.

value.zh: 匡周怒曰：「我在院中，故諸將不敢有異圖；
value.en: Kuang Zhou flared up: "While I am here, the generals dare not plot;
value.literal: Kuang Zhou angrily said: "While I am in the courtyard, therefore the generals dare not have divergent designs;

value.zh: 我出院，家必滅矣！」
value.en: if I leave, our house is finished!"
value.literal: if I leave the courtyard, the family will certainly be destroyed!"

value.zh: 稹固請之，匡周不得已，彈指而出。
value.en: Zhen insisted. Kuang Zhou had no choice: he snapped his fingers and walked out.
value.literal: Zhen firmly pressed him; Kuang Zhou had no choice, snapped his fingers, and went out.

value.zh: 誼令稹所親董可武說稹曰：「山東之叛，事由五舅，城中人人誰敢相保！
value.en: Yi had Zhen's confidant Dong Kewu tell him: "The Fifth Uncle caused the Shandong revolt. In this city, who can feel safe?
value.literal: Yi ordered Zhen's intimate Dong Kewu to persuade Zhen, saying: "The Shandong rebellion was caused by the Fifth Uncle; within the city, who dares guarantee anyone's safety!

value.zh: 留後今欲何如？」
value.en: What does the commissioner intend to do now?"
value.literal: What does the acting commissioner wish to do now?"

value.zh: 稹曰：「今城中尚有五萬人，且當閉門堅守耳。」
value.en: Zhen said: "We still have fifty thousand men in the city. We should shut the gates and hold on."
value.literal: Zhen said: "Now within the city there are still fifty thousand men; for the time being we should shut the gates and hold firm."

value.zh: 可武曰：「非良策也。
value.en: Kewu said: "That is no good plan.
value.literal: Kewu said: "That is not a good plan.

value.zh: 留後不若束身歸朝，如張元益，不失作刺史。
value.en: Better surrender yourself to the court, as Zhang Yuanyi did—you would still receive a prefecture.
value.literal: The acting commissioner would do better to bind himself and return to the court, like Zhang Yuanyi, and not fail to become a prefect.

value.zh: 且以郭誼為留後，俟得節之日，徐奉太夫人及室家金帛歸之東都，不亦善乎！」
value.en: Make Guo Yi acting commissioner for now. Once he receives the commission, your mother and family can take their wealth back to Luoyang in good time. Would that not be best?"
value.literal: Moreover appoint Guo Yi acting commissioner; when the day of receiving the commission arrives, slowly escort the Dowager Lady and the household's gold and silk back to the Eastern Capital—is that not also good!"

value.zh: 稹曰：「誼安肯如是？」
value.en: Zhen said: "Would Yi truly do that?"
value.literal: Zhen said: "How would Yi be willing to act thus?"

value.zh: 可武曰：「可武已與之重誓，必不負也。」
value.en: Kewu said: "I have sworn a solemn oath with him. He will not betray you."
value.literal: Kewu said: "Kewu has already sworn a heavy oath with him; he will certainly not betray you."

value.zh: 及引誼入。
value.en: Then he brought Yi in.
value.literal: Thereupon he led Yi in.

value.zh: 稹與之密約既定，乃白其母。
value.en: Once Zhen and Yi had sealed their secret pact, Zhen told his mother.
value.literal: After Zhen and he had set their secret agreement, he then informed his mother.

value.zh: 母曰：「歸朝誠為佳事，但恨已晚。
value.en: His mother said: "Surrender would indeed be wise, but I fear it is too late.
value.literal: His mother said: "Returning to the court is truly a fine matter, but I regret it is already late.

value.zh: 吾有弟不能保，安能保郭誼！
value.en: I could not even save my own brother—how can I trust Guo Yi!
value.literal: I could not even protect my own younger brother—how can I protect Guo Yi!

value.zh: 汝自圖之！」
value.en: You must decide for yourself!"
value.literal: You must plot for yourself!"

value.zh: 稹乃素服出門，以母命署誼都知兵馬使。
value.en: Zhen put on plain clothes, went out, and by his mother's authority appointed Yi commander of the army.
value.literal: Zhen then in plain dress went out the gate and, by his mother's order, appointed Yi commander of military affairs.

value.zh: 王協已戒諸將列於外廳，誼拜謝稹已，出見諸將，稹治裝於內廳。
value.en: Wang Xie had already assembled the generals in the outer hall. Yi bowed to Zhen, went out to face the officers, while Zhen packed in the inner hall.
value.literal: Wang Xie had already warned the generals to line up in the outer hall; after Yi bowed in thanks to Zhen, he went out to see the generals while Zhen packed in the inner hall.

value.zh: 李士貴聞之，帥後院兵數千攻誼。
value.en: Li Shigui heard of it and led several thousand household guards against Yi.
value.literal: Li Shigui heard this and led several thousand rear-courtyard troops to attack Yi.

value.zh: 誼叱之曰：「何不自取賞物，乃欲與李士貴同死乎！」
value.en: Yi shouted: "Why not seize your share of the loot instead of dying with Li Shigui!"
value.literal: Yi shouted at them: "Why not take reward goods for yourselves—do you wish to die together with Li Shigui!"

value.zh: 軍士乃退，共殺士貴。
value.en: The troops fell back and together killed Shigui.
value.literal: The soldiers then withdrew and together killed Shigui.

value.zh: 誼易置將吏，部署軍士，一夕俱定。
value.en: Yi replaced officers, redeployed the troops, and within a single night had everything under control.
value.literal: Yi replaced generals and officials, deployed the soldiers, and in one night all was settled.

value.zh: 明日，使董可武入謁稹曰：「請議公事。」
value.en: The next day he sent Dong Kewu to see Zhen: "We must discuss state business."
value.literal: The next day he sent Dong Kewu in to visit Zhen, saying: "I request to discuss official business."

value.zh: 稹曰：「何不言之！」
value.en: Zhen said: "Speak here, then!"
value.literal: Zhen said: "Why not speak of it!"

value.zh: 可武曰：「恐驚太夫人。」
value.en: Kewu said: "I fear distressing your mother."
value.literal: Kewu said: "I fear alarming the Dowager Lady."

value.zh: 乃引稹步出牙門，至北宅，置酒作樂。
value.en: He led Zhen on foot out through the headquarters gate to the North Residence, where wine and music were prepared.
value.literal: He then led Zhen on foot out the yamen gate to the North Residence, set out wine, and made music.

value.zh: 酒酣，乃言：「今日之事欲全太尉一家，須留後自圖去就，則朝廷必垂矜閔。」
value.en: When the wine had gone deep, he said: "To save your whole house, Commissioner, you must decide your own course. The court will surely show mercy."
value.literal: When the wine was deep, he then said: "Today's affair wishes to preserve the Grand Marshal's whole household; the acting commissioner must himself plot his going or staying—then the court will certainly extend pity."

value.zh: 稹曰：「如所言，稹之心也。」
