value.en: Zhen said: "What you say is exactly what I wish."
value.literal: Zhen said: "As you have said—that is Zhen's own heart."

value.zh: 可武遂前執其手，，崔率度自後斬之，因收稹宗族，匡周以下至襁褓中子皆殺之。
value.en: Kewu seized his hands from the front while Cui Shualv struck from behind and cut off his head. They then seized Zhen's entire clan and killed everyone from Kuang Zhou down to babes in arms.
value.literal: Kewu then stepped forward and seized his hand; Cui Shualv from behind beheaded him, then rounded up Zhen's clan—from Kuang Zhou down to infants still in swaddling clothes, all were killed.

value.zh: 又殺劉從諫父子所厚善者張谷、陳揚庭、李仲京、郭台、王羽、韓茂章、茂實、王渥、賈庠等凡十二家，並其子侄甥婿無遺。
value.en: They also slaughtered twelve households whom Liu Congjian and his son had favored—Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Guo Tai, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang and Maoshi, Wang Wo, Jia Xiang, and others—sparing not a son, nephew, son-in-law, or grandson.
value.literal: They also killed those whom Liu Congjian and his son had deeply favored—Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Guo Tai, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang, Maoshi, Wang Wo, Jia Xiang, and twelve households in all—together with their sons, nephews, sons-in-law, and sons of daughters, leaving none.

value.zh: 仲京，訓之兄；
value.en: Zhongjing was the elder brother of Li Xun;
value.literal: Zhongjing was Xun's elder brother;

value.zh: 台，行餘之子。
value.en: Guo Tai was the son of Guo Xingyu.
value.literal: Tai was Xingyu's son.

value.zh: 羽，涯之從孫；
value.en: Wang Yu was a collateral descendant of Wang Ya;
value.literal: Yu was Ya's collateral grandson;

value.zh: 茂章、茂實，約之子；
value.en: Han Maozhang and Maoshi were sons of Han Yue;
value.literal: Maozhang and Maoshi were Yue's sons;

value.zh: 渥，璠之子。
value.en: Wang Wo was the son of Wang Fan.
value.literal: Wo was Fan's son.

value.zh: 庠，餗之子也。
value.en: Jia Xiang was the son of Jia Su.
value.literal: Xiang was Su's son.

value.zh: 甘露之亂，仲京等亡歸從諫，從諫撫養之。
value.en: After the Sweet Dew Affair, Zhongjing and the others had fled to Liu Congjian, who sheltered and raised them.
value.literal: In the Sweet Dew turmoil, Zhongjing and the others fled and returned to Congjian, who nurtured them.

value.zh: 凡軍中有小嫌者，誼日有所誅，流血成泥。
value.en: Anyone in the army who bore the slightest grudge was put to death day after day until blood ran like mud.
value.literal: For anyone in the army with the slightest grudge, Yi daily executed some; blood flowed like mud.

value.zh: 乃函稹首，遣使奉表及書，降於王宰。
value.en: He placed Zhen's head in a box, sent envoys with a memorial and letter of surrender, and submitted to Wang Zai.
value.literal: He then boxed Zhen's head, sent envoys bearing a memorial and letter, and surrendered to Wang Zai.

value.zh: 首過澤州，劉公直舉營慟哭，亦降於宰。
value.en: As the head passed through Ze Prefecture, Liu Gongzhi led his entire camp in mourning and surrendered to Zai as well.
value.literal: When the head passed Ze Prefecture, Liu Gongzhi raised the whole camp in wailing lament and also surrendered to Zai.

value.zh: 乙未，宰以狀聞。
value.en: On the day yiwei, Zai reported the victory to the court.
value.literal: On the day yiwei, Zai reported the situation.

value.zh: 丙申，宰相入賀。
value.en: On the day bingshen, the chief ministers came in to offer congratulations.
value.literal: On the day bingshen, the chief ministers entered to congratulate.

value.zh: 李德裕奏：「今不須復置邢、洺、磁留後，但遣盧弘止宣慰三州及成德、魏博兩道。」
value.en: Li Deyu memorialized: "We need no longer appoint regents for Xing, Ming, and Ci. Send Lu Hongzhi to proclaim comfort to those three prefectures and to the Chengde and Weibo circuits."
value.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "Now there is no need again to appoint regents for Xing, Ming, and Ci; only send Lu Hongzhi to proclaim comfort to the three prefectures and the two circuits of Chengde and Weibo."

value.zh: 上曰：「郭誼宜如何處之？」
value.en: The Emperor asked: "What should be done with Guo Yi?"
value.literal: The Emperor said: "How should Guo Yi be dealt with?"

value.zh: 德裕對曰：「劉稹騃孺子耳，阻兵拒命，皆誼為之謀主。
value.en: Deyu answered: "Liu Zhen was a witless boy. Yi was the mastermind who armed the rebellion and defied the throne.
value.literal: Deyu replied: "Liu Zhen was but a foolish child; blocking troops and defying orders—all were plotted by Yi as chief strategist.

value.zh: 及勢孤力屈，又賣稹以求賞。
value.en: When his power collapsed, he sold out Zhen for a reward.
value.literal: When his position was isolated and strength exhausted, he again sold Zhen to seek reward.

value.zh: 此而不誅，何以懲惡！
value.en: If we spare him, how will we punish treachery!
value.literal: If this man is not executed, how can evil be punished!

value.zh: 宜及諸軍在境，並誼等誅之！」
value.en: Execute Yi and his accomplices while our armies are still on the ground!"
value.literal: It is fitting, while the various armies are still in the territory, to execute Yi and the rest together!"

value.zh: 上曰：「朕意亦以為然。」
value.en: The Emperor said: "I agree."
value.literal: The Emperor said: "My mind also holds it so."

value.zh: 乃詔石雄將七千人入潞州，以應謠言。
value.en: An edict ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand men into Lu Prefecture—fulfilling a popular prophecy.
value.literal: An edict then ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand men into Lu Prefecture, in accord with a popular saying.

value.zh: 杜悰以饋運不給，謂誼等可赦，上熟視不應。
value.en: Du Cong, citing supply shortages, argued that Yi and the others should be pardoned. The Emperor fixed him with a long stare and said nothing.
value.literal: Du Cong, because supply transport was insufficient, said Yi and the others could be pardoned; the Emperor stared at him intently and did not reply.

value.zh: 德裕曰：「今春澤潞未平，太原復擾，自非聖斷堅定，二寇何由可平！
value.en: Deyu said: "This spring Ze and Lu were still in revolt and Taiyuan was in turmoil again. Without Your Majesty's firm resolve, how could both rebellions have been crushed!
value.literal: Deyu said: "This spring Ze and Lu were not yet pacified, and Taiyuan was disturbed again—if not for Your Sagely resolve being firm, how could the two rebels have been subdued!

value.zh: 外議以為若在先朝，赦之久矣。」
value.en: Outsiders say that under the previous reign they would have been pardoned long ago."
value.literal: Outside opinion holds that under the previous reign they would long ago have been pardoned."

value.zh: 上曰：「卿不知文宗心地不與卿合，安能議乎！」
value.en: The Emperor said: "You forget that Emperor Wenzong's mind was not yours. How could he have acted as you would!"
value.literal: The Emperor said: "You do not know that Emperor Wenzong's mind was not in accord with yours—how could he have deliberated thus!"

value.zh: 罷盧鈞山南東道，專為昭義節度使。
value.en: Lu Jun was relieved of Shannan East and appointed solely military governor of Zhaoyi.
value.literal: Lu Jun was removed from Shannan East Circuit and made solely military governor of Zhaoyi.

value.zh: 戊戌，劉稹傳首至京師。
value.en: On the day wuxu, Liu Zhen's head arrived at the capital.
value.literal: On the day wuxu, Liu Zhen's transmitted head reached the capital.

value.zh: 詔：「昭義五州給復一年，軍行所過州縣免今年秋稅。
value.en: An edict declared: "The five Zhaoyi prefectures shall receive a year's tax relief, and every county and prefecture the army passed through is exempt from this autumn's levy.
value.literal: An edict: "The five prefectures of Zhaoyi shall receive tax relief for one year; prefectures and counties through which the army passed are exempted from this year's autumn tax.

value.zh: 昭義自劉從諫以來，橫增賦斂，悉從蠲免。
value.en: All arbitrary levies imposed since Liu Congjian's day were abolished.
value.literal: Since Liu Congjian's time Zhaoyi had arbitrarily increased levies—all are remitted from exemption.

value.zh: 所藉土團並縱遣歸農。
value.en: Conscripted local militia were disbanded and sent home to farm.
value.literal: Local militia that had been conscripted were all released and sent back to farming.

value.zh: 諸道將士有功者，等級加賞。」
value.en: Meritorious officers and soldiers from every circuit were rewarded according to rank."
value.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various circuits who had merit received graded additional rewards."

value.zh: 郭誼既殺劉稹，日望旌節，既久不聞問，乃曰：「必移它鎮。」
value.en: After killing Liu Zhen, Guo Yi waited daily for his commission as military governor. When no word came for a long time, he said: "They must be transferring me to another circuit."
value.literal: After Guo Yi had killed Liu Zhen, he daily looked for the commission of office; having long heard nothing, he then said: "I must surely be transferred to another post."

value.zh: 於是閱鞍馬，治行裝。
value.en: He inspected his horses and packed for the journey.
value.literal: He then inspected saddles and horses and prepared traveling gear.

value.zh: 及聞石雄將至，懼失色。
value.en: When he learned that Shi Xiong was coming, he turned pale with fear.
value.literal: When he heard Shi Xiong was about to arrive, he turned pale with fear.

value.zh: 雄至，誼等參賀畢，敕使張仲清曰：「郭都知告身來日當至，諸高班告身在此，晚牙來受之！」
value.en: When Xiong arrived, Yi and the others paid their respects. The imperial envoy Zhang Zhongqing announced: "Commander Guo's commission will arrive tomorrow. The senior officers' commissions are here—come to the evening assembly to receive them!"
value.literal: When Xiong arrived, after Yi and the others had paid their respects, the edict envoy Zhang Zhongqing said: "Commander Guo's commission of appointment will arrive tomorrow; the senior officers' commissions are here—come receive them at the evening roll call!"

value.zh: 乃以河中兵環球場，晚牙，誼等至，唱名引入，凡諸將桀黠拒官軍者，悉執送京師。
value.en: Hezhong troops ringed the parade ground. At the evening assembly, as Yi and the others arrived, their names were called and they were led in. Every fierce commander who had resisted the imperial army was seized and sent to the capital.
value.literal: He then had Hezhong troops surround the ball ground; at evening roll call, when Yi and the others arrived, names were called and they were led in—all fierce and cunning generals who had resisted government troops were seized and sent to the capital.

value.zh: 加何弘敬同平章事。
value.en: He Hongjing was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
value.literal: He Hongjing was promoted to Associate Director of the Chancellery.

value.zh: 丁未，詔發劉從諫屍，暴於潞州市三日，石雄取其屍置球場斬坐刀之。
value.en: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered Liu Congjian's corpse exhumed and displayed in Lu Prefecture for three days. Shi Xiong then had the body brought to the parade ground and executed by waist-slicing in the seated position.
value.literal: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered Liu Congjian's corpse exhumed and exposed in Lu Prefecture city for three days; Shi Xiong took the corpse, placed it on the ball ground, and executed it by seated waist-slicing.

value.zh: 丁巳，盧鈞入潞州。
value.en: On the day dingsi, Lu Jun entered Lu Prefecture.
value.literal: On the day dingsi, Lu Jun entered Lu Prefecture.

value.zh: 鈞素寬厚愛人，劉稹未平，鈞已領昭義節度，襄州士卒在行營者，與潞人戰，常對陳揚鈞之美。
value.en: Jun was known for his generosity and kindness. Even before Liu Zhen fell, he had been appointed military governor of Zhaoyi, and Xiang soldiers in the field camp often praised his virtues to the Lu troops across the battle lines.
value.literal: Jun was by nature generous and loving toward people; before Liu Zhen was pacified, Jun already held the Zhaoyi military governorship, and Xiang Prefecture soldiers in the field camp, when fighting Lu men, often praised Jun's virtues across the battle lines.

value.zh: 及赴鎮，入天井關，昭義散卒歸之道，鈞皆厚撫之，人情大洽，昭議遂安。
value.en: When he went to take up his post and entered Tianjing Pass, he generously treated every scattered Zhaoyi soldier he met on the road. Hearts warmed to him, and Zhaoyi was soon at peace.
value.literal: When he went to his post and entered Tianjing Pass, Zhaoyi scattered soldiers returning on the road were all generously comforted by Jun; popular sentiment was greatly harmonious, and Zhaoyi was thereby settled.

value.zh: 劉稹將郭誼、王協、劉公直、安全慶、李道德、劉佐堯、劉開德、董可武等至京師，皆斬之。
value.en: Liu Zhen's generals Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Quanqing, Li Daode, Liu Zuoyao, Liu Kaide, Dong Kewu, and others were brought to the capital and all beheaded.
value.literal: Liu Zhen's generals Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Quanqing, Li Daode, Liu Zuoyao, Liu Kaide, Dong Kewu, and others reached the capital—all were beheaded.

value.zh: 臣光曰：董重質之在淮西，郭誼之在昭義，吳元濟、劉稹，如木偶人在伎兒之手耳。
value.en: Sima Guang comments: With Dong Chongzhi in Huaixi and Guo Yi in Zhaoyi, Wu Yuanji and Liu Zhen were no more than wooden puppets in the hands of puppeteers.
value.literal: Your subject Guang says: With Dong Chongzhi in Huaixi and Guo Yi in Zhaoyi, Wu Yuanji and Liu Zhen were like wooden puppets in the hands of showmen.

value.zh: 彼二人者，始則勸人為亂，終則賣主規利，其死固有餘罪。
value.en: Those two men first incited rebellion and then betrayed their masters for gain. Their deaths were richly deserved.
value.literal: Those two men at first urged others to rebel, and in the end sold their masters to seek profit; their deaths indeed left guilt to spare.

value.zh: 然憲宗用之於前，武宗誅之於後，臣愚以為皆失之。
value.en: Yet Emperor Xianzong used them before, and Emperor Wuzong executed them after. In my humble view, both rulers were wrong.
value.literal: Yet Emperor Xianzong employed them before, and Emperor Wuzong executed them after—I, your foolish subject, hold that both were in error.

value.zh: 何則？
value.en: Why so?
value.literal: Why?

value.zh: 賞奸，非義也；
value.en: To reward traitors is unjust;
value.literal: Rewarding the wicked is not righteous;

value.zh: 殺降，非信也。
value.en: to kill men who have surrendered is faithless.
value.literal: killing those who surrender is not faithful.

value.zh: 失義與信，何以為國！
value.en: Without righteousness and faith, how can a state endure!
value.literal: Losing righteousness and faith—how can one be a state!

value.zh: 昔漢光武待王郎、劉盆子止於不死，知其非力竭則不降故也。
value.en: Emperor Guangwu of Han spared Wang Lang and Liu Penzi only their lives, knowing that rebels surrender only when their strength is spent.
value.literal: Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han treated Wang Lang and Liu Penzi only to the point of not killing them, knowing that unless strength was exhausted they would not surrender.

value.zh: 樊崇、徐宣、王元、牛邯之徒，豈非助亂之人乎？
value.en: Were Fan Chong, Xu Xuan, Wang Yuan, Niu Han, and their like not agents of rebellion?
value.literal: Fan Chong, Xu Xuan, Wang Yuan, Niu Han, and their kind—were they not men who aided rebellion?

value.zh: 而光武弗殺。
value.en: Yet Guangwu did not execute them.
value.literal: Yet Guangwu did not kill them.

value.zh: 蓋以既受其降，則不可復誅故也。
value.en: Once he had accepted their surrender, he could not put them to death.
value.literal: This was because once their surrender had been accepted, they could not again be executed.

value.zh: 若既赦而復逃亡叛亂，則其死固無辭矣！
value.en: If, after pardon, they fled and rebelled again, execution would be fully justified!
value.literal: If after pardon they again fled, rebelled, and made turmoil, then their death would indeed admit no excuse!

value.zh: 如誼等，免死流之遠方，沒齒不還，可矣；
value.en: Men like Yi should have been spared and exiled to distant lands, never to return—that would have been enough;
value.literal: Men like Yi could have been spared death and exiled to distant regions, never to return within their lives—that would have sufficed;

value.zh: 殺之，非也！
value.en: to kill them was wrong!
value.literal: to kill them was wrong!

value.zh: 王羽、賈庠等已為誼所殺，李德裕復下詔稱「逆賊王涯、賈餗等已就昭義誅其子孫」，宣告中外，識者非之。
value.en: Wang Yu, Jia Xiang, and the others had already been killed by Yi. Li Deyu then issued an edict proclaiming to all within and without that "the rebel criminals Wang Ya, Jia Su, and others have had their descendants executed in Zhaoyi." Thoughtful men condemned this.
value.literal: Wang Yu, Jia Xiang, and the others had already been killed by Yi; Li Deyu again issued an edict stating "the rebel criminals Wang Ya, Jia Su, and others have already had their descendants executed at Zhaoyi," proclaiming it within and without—men of judgment disapproved.

value.zh: 劉從諫妻裴氏亦賜死。
value.en: Liu Congjian's widow Lady Pei was also ordered to take her own life.
value.literal: Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was also ordered to die.

value.zh: 又令昭義降將李丕、高文端、王釗等疏昭義將士與劉稹同惡者，悉誅之，死者甚眾。
value.en: He also had Zhaoyi defectors Li Pi, Gao Wenduan, Wang Zhao, and others denounce every officer and soldier who had sided with Liu Zhen. All were executed, and the dead were very numerous.
value.literal: He also ordered Zhaoyi surrendering generals Li Pi, Gao Wenduan, Wang Zhao, and others to denounce Zhaoyi officers and soldiers who shared Liu Zhen's evil—all were executed, and the dead were very many.

value.zh: 盧鈞疑其枉濫，奏請寬之，不從。
value.en: Lu Jun suspected wholesale injustice and memorialized for clemency, but the court refused.
value.literal: Lu Jun suspected this was excessive and indiscriminate, memorialized asking leniency, and was not followed.

value.zh: 昭義屬城有嘗無禮於王元逵者，元逵推求得二十餘人，斬之。
value.en: In one Zhaoyi subordinate city, men who had once insulted Wang Yuankui were hunted down; he beheaded more than twenty of them.
value.literal: In a subordinate city of Zhaoyi there were those who had once been disrespectful to Wang Yuankui; Yuankui tracked them down and got more than twenty men, whom he beheaded.

value.zh: 餘眾懼，復閉城自守。
value.en: The rest of the populace, terrified, shut the gates and held the city again.
value.literal: The remaining multitude were afraid and again closed the city to hold it themselves.

value.zh: 戊辰，李德裕等奏：「寇孽既平，盡為國家城鎮，豈可令元逵窮兵攻討！
value.en: On the day wuchen, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The rebels are crushed and these are imperial towns. How can we let Yuankui press the attack to the bitter end!
value.literal: On the day wuchen, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The rebel brood being already pacified, all are the state's towns and cities—how can Yuankui be allowed to exhaust troops in attack!

value.zh: 望遣中使賜城內將士敕，招安之，仍詔元逵引兵歸鎮，並詔盧鈞自遣使安撫。」
value.en: Send a palace envoy with an edict to reassure the garrison, order Yuankui to withdraw to his post, and let Lu Jun send his own envoys to pacify them."
value.literal: We hope to send a palace envoy to grant an edict to the city's officers and soldiers and win them by reassurance, and also order Yuankui to lead troops back to his post, and order Lu Jun on his own to send envoys to pacify."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The court agreed.
value.literal: This was followed.

value.zh: 李德裕怨太子太傅、東都留守牛僧孺、湖州刺史李宗閔，言於上曰：「劉從諫據上黨十年，太和中入朝，僧孺、宗閔執政，不留之，加宰相縱去，以成今日之患，竭天下力乃能取之，皆二人之罪也。」
value.en: Li Deyu bore a grudge against Niu Sengru, Grand Mentor and regent of the Eastern Capital, and Li Zongmin, prefect of Huzhou. He told the Emperor: "Liu Congjian held Shangdang for ten years. During the Taihe era he came to court while Sengru and Zongmin were in power. They did not detain him but made him chief minister and let him return—creating today's disaster. Only by exhausting the empire's strength could we recover the region. The fault lies with those two men."
value.literal: Li Deyu resented Grand Mentor and Eastern Capital regent Niu Sengru and Huzhou Prefect Li Zongmin, and said to the Emperor: "Liu Congjian held Shangdang for ten years; in the Taihe era he entered court—Sengru and Zongmin held government, did not detain him, added him as chief minister and let him go, thereby creating today's calamity; exhausting the empire's strength was needed to take it—all is the crime of those two men."

value.zh: 德裕又使人於潞州求僧孺、宗閔與從諫交通書疏，無所得，乃令孔目官鄭慶言從諫每得僧孺、宗閔書疏，皆自焚毀。
value.en: Deyu also sent men to Lu Prefecture to search for correspondence between Sengru, Zongmin, and Congjian. Finding none, he had a clerk named Zheng Qing claim that Congjian had burned every letter he received from Sengru and Zongmin.
value.literal: Deyu also sent men to Lu Prefecture to seek correspondence between Sengru, Zongmin, and Congjian; obtaining none, he then had clerical officer Zheng Qing say that whenever Congjian received letters from Sengru and Zongmin he burned them himself.

value.zh: 詔追慶下御史台近問，中丞李回、知雜鄭亞以為信然。
value.en: An edict ordered Qing brought before the Censorate for interrogation. Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Supervisory Censor Zheng Ya found his testimony credible.
value.literal: An edict ordered Qing pursued to the Censorate for close interrogation; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Supervisory Censor Zheng Ya held it credible.

value.zh: 河南少尹呂述與德裕書，言稹破報至，僧孺出聲歎恨。
value.en: Lü Shu, vice prefect of Henan, wrote to Deyu that when news of Liu Zhen's defeat arrived, Niu Sengru sighed aloud in regret.
value.literal: Henan Vice Prefect Lü Shu wrote to Deyu, saying that when the report of Zhen's defeat arrived, Sengru gave voice to sighs of regret.

value.zh: 德裕奏述書，上大怒，以僧孺為太子少保、分司，宗閔為漳州刺史。
value.en: Deyu submitted a memorial recounting Lü Shu's letter. The emperor flew into a rage and made Niu Sengru Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal court post, and Li Zongmin prefect of Zhang Prefecture.
value.literal: Deyu memorialized describing Shu's letter; the emperor was greatly angered and made Sengru Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal post, and Zongmin Prefect of Zhang Prefecture.

value.zh: 戊子，再貶僧孺汀州刺史，宗閔漳州長史。
value.en: On wuzi, Sengru was demoted again to prefect of Ting Prefecture, and Zongmin to chief secretary of Zhang Prefecture.
value.literal: On wuzi, Sengru was demoted again to Prefect of Ting Prefecture, Zongmin to Chief Secretary of Zhang Prefecture.
